question:
A Java app uses Hibernate against PostgreSQL. It is supposed to persist a new MyClass entity, but the row never shows up in the table. No exception or error is raised.

With SQL logging turned on, the last statement printed for the save is:

```
Hibernate: select nextval('hibernate_sequence')
```

After that, no further SQL appears. To the developer, it looks like Hibernate is stuck at that point.

The mapping file:

```
<class name="src.MyClass" table="MyClass">
 <cache usage="read-write"/>
 <id name="id" column="classid"><generator class="native"/></id>
 <property name="name" column="name" not-null="true" unique="true" length="160"/>
</class>
```

The DAO method:

```
public void save(Myclass mc) {
 Session session = sessionFactory.getCurrentSession();
 session.save(mc);
}
```

Things already checked:
- Reading data with SELECT through Hibernate works fine.
- A native SQL INSERT run manually against the same database succeeds.

Why are the saved objects not reaching the database?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The code calls session.save() but never flushes the session or commits a transaction. Hibernate only fetches the id from the sequence and keeps the INSERT queued, so it is never executed against the database. Fix: Wrap the save in a transaction: open a session, call beginTransaction(), then save(mc), then tx.commit(), which flushes automatically. Roll back on exceptions and close the session in a finally block. At a minimum, call session.flush() after save.
solution: (1) session.save() alone does not execute the INSERT immediately; it only obtains the id (the nextval call) (2) No flush or transaction commit is performed, so pending SQL is never sent (3) The fix is to commit a transaction (or flush) after save

grounding.title: Hibernate not saving Object in the Database?

question:
Deploying a single-replica MongoDB Deployment on a local Minikube cluster. The pod sits in CrashLoopBackOff (6 restarts in ~8 minutes). Several image tags were tried (mongo:latest, 5.0.0, 4.0) and every one fails the same way. Startup logs show the init fork ("about to fork child process, waiting until server is ready"), then mongod 4.4.6 starting on Ubuntu 18.04 bound to 127.0.0.1. During the root-user init step the container dies with a U_STRINGPREP_PROHIBITED_ERROR.

The root credentials are passed as MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME and MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD, both read from an Opaque Secret through secretKeyRef. The Secret was written by hand with pre-encoded base64 values under data:

  mongo-root-username: dXNlcm5hbWUNCg==
  mongo-root-password: cGFzc3dvcmQNCg==

The Deployment selector and template labels match (app: mongodb). The Secret and Deployment were re-applied several times, which created multiple ReplicaSets. None of them became ready.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer:
Root cause: The base64 values in the Secret decode to 'username
' and 'password
'. They were encoded with Windows-style CRLF line endings, so the username and password passed to MongoDB contain non-printable characters that SASLprep/stringprep rejects. Fix: Re-create the Secret with values that have no trailing  or 
. For example, encode them with `echo -n`, or use the stringData field with the plain values (mongo-root-username: username, mongo-root-password: password) and let Kubernetes do the encoding. Then redeploy.
solution: (1) Decoding the secret values shows trailing \r\n (^M$) characters (2) The credentials were base64-encoded including CRLF line endings (3) MongoDB stringprep rejects the prohibited control characters in the username/password (4) Re-create the secret without newline/CR, e.g. using stringData or echo -n

grounding.title: Getting U_STRINGPREP_PROHIBITED_ERROR when trying to deploy MongoDB on Kubernetes

question:
After a full OS and software reinstall on my workstation, a Django project that ran fine before now breaks on many pages. The same code works on a colleague's machine and on the dev server. PostgreSQL is now 8.4; it was 8.3 before, though I'm not sure the old install was ever tested on 8.4.

The debug page shows:

TemplateSyntaxError at /
Caught an exception while rendering: current transaction is aborted, commands ignored until end of transaction block

The failing template variables and custom tags all touch the database somewhere, but not every DB-touching tag fails, and some pages render fine. When I remove the variable or tag the error points to, a different one starts failing. After I remove all of them, I get a blank white page. Its traceback runs through debug_toolbar's process_response and render_toolbar, then render_to_string, and down into the template rendering nodes.

Is Django incompatible with PostgreSQL 8.4, or is something else going on?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: An earlier SQL statement in the same request failed, possibly one not visible on the error page. Django runs the request's queries inside a single database transaction, so after that first error PostgreSQL rejects every following statement until the transaction ends. The template errors are a symptom of that first failure, not of a Django/8.4 incompatibility or a template problem. Fix: Tail the PostgreSQL error log (e.g. tail -f /path/to/postgresql log) while refreshing the page to find the first SQL statement that actually errors. Then fix that query or the schema mismatch behind it.
solution: (1) The error means a prior SQL statement in the transaction failed (2) PostgreSQL ignores all subsequent statements in an aborted transaction until it ends (3) The template tags reported are not the real cause; whichever DB access comes next fails (4) Check the PostgreSQL server log to find the original failing query

grounding.title: Django TemplateSyntaxError: current transaction is aborted, what does this exception mean? Does postgresql 8.4 work fine with django?

question:
We run a Scala Kafka Streams app on Kubernetes as a StatefulSet. Each replica uses its own applicationId, so every consumer group has exactly one Streams instance. Each instance reads a state topic into a RocksDB state store and serves REST queries from it. During a rolling restart, each pod takes about 5 minutes to come back. Almost all of that time it sits in REBALANCING state, even though it restarts with the same applicationId. We expected it to resume where it left off almost immediately. Settings changed from defaults: consumer max.poll.records=1000, consumer session.timeout.ms=300000 (raised because the brokers are in another data center and the network is flaky), auto.offset.reset=earliest, and a bounded-memory RocksDB config setter. max.poll.interval.ms and group.initial.rebalance.delay.ms are at their defaults. The brokers are an older version that does not support group.instance.id. We want to know why the restart rebalance takes so long and which settings control it.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: Kafka Streams does not send a LeaveGroupRequest on shutdown, so the coordinator keeps the old member until session.timeout.ms expires, which is 5 minutes here. The restarted pod joins as a new member, and the rebalance cannot finish until the old member times out. To the coordinator it looks like the group is growing from one member to two. Fix: Lower session.timeout.ms (for example to about 3 minutes) so the stale member expires sooner. The better fix is to upgrade the brokers and use static group membership (group.instance.id, KIP-345), so the restarted instance is recognized as the old member and no rebalance wait occurs.
solution: (1) No LeaveGroupRequest is sent on shutdown, so the old member remains in the group (2) The old member is only removed after session.timeout.ms (300000 ms, about 5 minutes) expires (3) The restarted instance is treated as a new member and the rebalance waits for the old one to expire (4) Lowering session.timeout.ms or using static membership via group.instance.id fixes it

grounding.title: Kafka Streams on Kubernetes: Long rebalancing after redeployment

question:
We're extending the official joomla:3.9-php7.2-apache image so we can ship our site files in it. The Dockerfile installs a few packages with apt (that works). It then COPYs ./joomla_html into /var/www/html, which also works because the files show up. After that come a series of RUN steps: `chmod -R 765 /var/www/html/`, `chown -R www-data. /var/www/html/`, and `chmod -R 777` on tmp, modules, components, administrator/logs, images and uploads. Last, it copies a php.ini into /usr/local/etc/php/conf.d/. The build finishes without errors.

When we run the container, every file under /var/www/html is still owned by 1000:1000 with the original modes:
```
drwxr-xr-x 19 1000 1000 4096 May 8 18:53 .
drwxr-xr-x 25 1000 1000 4096 May 8 18:53 components
drwxr-xr-x 68 1000 1000 4096 May 8 18:53 modules
drwxr-xr-x 2 1000 1000 4096 May 8 18:53 tmp
...
```
The chmod and chown steps seem to do nothing, but every other instruction in the Dockerfile takes effect. We need the files owned by www-data. Why are those changes being lost?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The upstream joomla base image declares `VOLUME /var/www/html`. A RUN step runs in a temporary container where that path is a volume, and only changes to the container filesystem are saved, not changes inside the volume. COPY still works because it writes directly to the image filesystem. Fix: Remove the VOLUME definition by rebuilding the base image yourself or asking upstream to drop it. Otherwise, stage the files in another directory and copy them into /var/www/html from an entrypoint at startup. A third option is a multi-stage build: fix permissions in the first stage, then COPY the files (with --chown if needed) into /var/www/html in the final stage.
solution: (1) The base image Dockerfile declares VOLUME /var/www/html (2) RUN changes to a path declared as a volume are discarded and not saved in the image layer (3) COPY writes directly into the image filesystem, so the copied files appear but chmod/chown via RUN do not (4) Fix permissions outside the volume path, e.g. in a multi-stage build or an entrypoint, or remove the VOLUME from the base image

grounding.title: Dockerfile "RUN chmod" not taking effect

answer: Root cause: @SequenceGenerator defaults to an allocationSize (increment) of 50. Hibernate therefore treats the sequence value as a hi/lo-style seed for a block of IDs instead of using it directly. That is why 1604 becomes 1554 (1604 - 50), which does not match a database sequence that increments by 1. Fix: Set allocationSize = 1 on the @SequenceGenerator so it matches the sequence's increment of 1. On newer Hibernate releases, you can alternatively set hibernate.id.new_generator_mappings=true.
solution: (1) @SequenceGenerator has a default allocationSize of 50. (2) Hibernate uses the sequence value as a hi/lo seed for a block of IDs rather than as the literal ID. (3) The generated ID is offset from the sequence value by the allocation size: 1604 - 50 = 1554. (4) Fix: set allocationSize=1 to match the DB sequence increment, or set hibernate.id.new_generator_mappings=true.

grounding.title: Hibernate generating two different sequence Ids for PostgreSQL insert

question:
On my Mac I'm running Docker through a docker-machine VM so I can mount my working source tree into a container for live development. The Dockerfile is minimal:

FROM python:3.5.1
WORKDIR /var/dynamo
RUN pip3 install tornado
EXPOSE 8001

I start it from the project directory with:
docker run -v $(pwd):/var/dynamo -d -t -p 8001:8001 --name dynamo davesrepo/dynamo

The container runs. When I exec in (docker exec -it dynamo /bin/bash) and run ls -la in /var/dynamo, the directory is empty: total 4, only . and .. (drwxr-xr-x 2 root root 40). docker inspect looks correct. HostConfig.Binds shows "/Users/dave/Sites/davesrepo/dynamo:/var/dynamo" and Mounts shows Source /Users/dave/Sites/davesrepo/dynamo, Destination /var/dynamo, RW true. Other paths in the inspect output include ResolvConfPath under /mnt/sda1/var/lib/docker/containers/... and the storage driver is aufs. The host directory definitely contains my project files (Dockerfile, README.md, config.ini, tests, etc.). Why is the mounted directory empty?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: With docker-machine on macOS, the Docker daemon runs inside a VirtualBox VM, and bind-mount source paths are resolved inside that VM. The VM's VirtualBox shared folder for /Users was not set up correctly, so /Users/dave/... inside the VM was missing or empty, and Docker bind-mounted an empty directory. Fix: Recreate the docker-machine VM so the /Users directory is properly shared from VirtualBox: docker-machine stop dev; docker-machine rm dev; docker-machine create --driver virtualbox dev; eval "$(docker-machine env dev)". Then rebuild the image and rerun the container with the same -v $(pwd):/var/dynamo mount. The project files will then appear.
solution: (1) The Docker daemon runs inside a docker-machine/VirtualBox VM, not directly on macOS (2) The -v host path is resolved inside the VM, which only sees host files through VirtualBox shared folders (/Users) (3) The /Users shared folder was not set up correctly, so the bind source in the VM was empty even though docker inspect looked correct (4) Recreating the docker-machine VM with /Users shared properly fixes the empty mount
technology: Docker / docker-machine with VirtualBox on macOS

grounding.title: Docker Volume not mounting any files

question:
We're containerizing a small Java server that runs fine with `gradle run` on the host (Gradle 4.3.1, JDK 8). Docker runs through docker-machine 0.13.0 with a VirtualBox VM. The Dockerfile is:

```
FROM gradle:4.3-jdk-alpine
ADD . /code
WORKDIR /code
CMD ["gradle", "--stacktrace", "run"]
```

`docker build -t my-server-app .` completes with no errors. Running `docker run --rm my-server-app` fails right away:

```
Could not create service of type ScriptPluginFactory using BuildScopeServices.createScriptPluginFactory().
> Could not create service of type CrossBuildFileHashCache using BuildSessionScopeServices.createCrossBuildFileHashCache().
...
Caused by: org.gradle.api.UncheckedIOException: Failed to create parent directory '/code/.gradle/4.3' when creating directory '/code/.gradle/4.3/fileHashes'
  at org.gradle.util.GFileUtils.mkdirs(GFileUtils.java:271)
```

All tools are current versions. Why can't Gradle create this directory inside the container?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The official gradle base image runs as the non-root user `gradle`. The project files added to /code with ADD are owned by root, so Gradle has no write permission there and cannot create its `.gradle` cache directory. Fix: Change ownership of the copied files to the gradle user, e.g. `ADD --chown=gradle . /code`. Another option is to use a directory the gradle user can already write to, such as /home/gradle.
solution: (1) The gradle image runs as user `gradle`, not root (2) ADD/COPY creates the files as root-owned by default (3) Gradle needs write access to create /code/.gradle (4) Use `--chown=gradle` on ADD/COPY or use a gradle-writable directory

grounding.title: Running simple Java Gradle app in Docker

question:
A Java service generates Word documents with a third-party library. Its image is built from a minimal Dockerfile: FROM openjdk:10-jdk-slim, copy the jar to /opt/, then run java -jar.

When a developer builds locally (mvn package, then docker build on Docker for Mac) and deploys to Kubernetes, everything works.

When the image comes from the Jenkins pipeline, one document-generation path fails at runtime. In that pipeline, Maven runs in maven:3.5.4-jdk-10-slim and docker build runs via a docker:dind container. The error is:

Caused by: java.lang.NullPointerException: null
 at java.desktop/sun.awt.FontConfiguration.getVersion(FontConfiguration.java:1288)
 at java.desktop/sun.awt.FontConfiguration.readFontConfigFile(FontConfiguration.java:225)
 at java.desktop/sun.awt.FontConfiguration.init(FontConfiguration.java:107)
 at java.desktop/sun.awt.X11FontManager.createFontConfiguration(X11FontManager.java:765)
 at java.desktop/sun.font.SunFontManager.<init>(SunFontManager.java:385)

What has been checked so far:
- The jar files from both builds have identical class files.
- Both images use the same FROM line.
- In the locally built image, ls -l /usr/lib shows X11, dbus-1.0, dconf, glib-networking, cgmanager, libnih*, systemd and similar entries. The Jenkins-built image's /usr/lib listing is noticeably sparser.
- docker info on the Mac reports 'Docker for Mac' with a linuxkit kernel. On Jenkins it reports 'Alpine Linux v3.7 (containerized)'.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The image produced by the Jenkins/docker:dind build does not contain fontconfig or the related font and X11 support libraries that the locally built image happened to have. The JDK's AWT FontConfiguration therefore finds no font configuration and throws an NPE when the document library initializes fonts. Fix: Install the font packages explicitly in the Dockerfile so the image does not depend on the build environment, e.g. RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y fontconfig. The answer also installed dbus, glib-networking, dconf-cli and similar packages.
solution: (1) The jar is identical; the difference is in the built image's OS packages, not the code (2) The CI-built image lacks fontconfig and font libraries that the local image had (3) The JDK's sun.awt.FontConfiguration NPEs when no font configuration is available (4) Fix by explicitly installing fontconfig (and related libs) via apt-get in the Dockerfile

grounding.title: Docker and Java - FontConfiguration issue

question:
We are on Windows 10 running Docker 17.06.0-ce with the VirtualBox driver (docker-machine IP 192.168.99.100). I started three mongo:3.6.0 containers on a user-defined network 'mongo-cluster', each with `mongod --replSet my-mongo-set`. Host ports are published as 9042, 9142 and 9242, all mapping to 27017.

From inside mongo1 I ran rs.initiate with members mongo1:27017, mongo2:27017 and mongo3:27017. The container logs show all members connected and healthy.

Our Java app uses mongodb-driver 3.6.0. It builds a MongoClient from a list of three ServerAddress entries: 192.168.99.100 on ports 9042, 9142 and 9242. The driver log shows:
- "Cluster created with settings {hosts=[192.168.99.100:9042, ...], mode=MULTIPLE}"
- "Opened connection" to all three addresses
- "Monitor thread successfully connected to server with description ServerDescription{address=192.168.99.100:9242, type=R..."

After that, the log fills with MongoSocketException errors for mongo1:27017, mongo2:27017 and mongo3:27017. Operations fail when server selection times out after 30000 ms. The seed connections clearly succeed, so why can't the app use the cluster?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: After connecting to the seed addresses, the driver follows the replica set spec and switches to the hostnames listed in the replica set config (mongo1, mongo2, mongo3). Those Docker-internal container names do not resolve and are not reachable from the Windows host, which can only see the VirtualBox VM IP. Fix: Make the replica set config hostnames resolvable from the client. Add entries to C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts mapping mongo1, mongo2 and mongo3 to the Docker VM IP 192.168.99.100.
solution: (1) The driver uses the hostnames from the replica set config, not the seed list addresses (2) The member hostnames mongo1/mongo2/mongo3 exist only on the Docker network and cannot be resolved from the Windows host (3) Hostnames in the replica set config must be reachable from the client (4) The fix is hosts-file entries mapping those names to the VM IP 192.168.99.100
technology: MongoDB replica set, Docker (VirtualBox on Windows), MongoDB Java driver

grounding.title: Connect to MongoDB Replica Set running inside Docker with Java (Windows)

question:
Our Django app runs in a Rancher-managed container on a cloud VPS. For a few weeks outgoing email has failed with timeout errors. We relay through Mailgun's SMTP service. Inside the container, Python 2.7.14 (python:2.7-alpine image):

  from smtplib import SMTP
  smtp = SMTP(host='smtp.mailgun.org', port=587)

This hangs. With a timeout set, it raises a timeout. The exact same image tag, run locally with `docker run -ti registry.gitlab.com/namespace/app:<commit-hash> /bin/sh`, connects right away. Mailgun support says they are not blocking our production IP and suggested we check our own configuration. The only difference between environments is some app-level env variables. We also removed gevent, but that changed nothing.

From the container console:
  telnet smtp.mailgun.org 587
  telnet: can't connect to remote host (52.10.40.100): Operation timed out

From the VPS host itself, outside Docker:
  telnet smtp.mailgun.org 587
  Trying 34.232.180.42...
  Trying 54.164.235.211...
  Trying 34.237.7.101...
  telnet: Unable to connect to remote host: Connection timed out

What is preventing the SMTP connection?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The hosting provider (Scaleway) blocks outbound SMTP ports on the server by default, pending account verification. Connections to the external SMTP relay therefore time out from both the host and the container. Neither Docker, the image, nor Mailgun is the cause. Fix: Complete the hosting provider's account verification and disable the SMTP port block in its settings. Then hard-reboot the server so the change takes effect.
solution: (1) The failure also occurs on the host outside Docker, so the container and image are not the cause. (2) The same image works from another network, which points to the server's network or provider. (3) The cloud/hosting provider (Scaleway) blocks outbound SMTP ports by default. (4) The fix is to verify the account, remove the block with the provider, and reboot the server.

grounding.title: smtp timeout from python client in rancher container

question:
Our ~20 IIS AppPools use the ServiceStack C# Redis client. Each AppPool holds a singleton PooledRedisClientManager with read and write pool sizes of 50. They connect over the public IP to a single Redis 2.6 instance on Ubuntu 12.04, an 8GB Rackspace Cloud VM. The connection is password protected. Every operation wraps client usage in `using (var client = ClientManager.GetClient())`.

Relevant redis.conf settings:
- timeout 300
- save 900 1 / save 300 10 / save 60 10000
- rdbcompression yes
- maxclients 10000
- maxmemory 7gb
- maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru
- appendonly no

File descriptor limits were raised to 10240. Expected peak is about 2000-4000 connections.

Things mostly work. However, the logs repeatedly show bursts of a few hundred of these errors at once, then nothing for about an hour, then another burst:

```
System.IO.IOException: Unable to read data from the transport connection: An existing connection was forcibly closed by the remote host.
---> System.Net.Sockets.SocketException ... at System.Net.Sockets.Socket.Receive(...)
 at ServiceStack.Redis.RedisNativeClient.ReadLine() RedisNativeClient_Utils.cs:line 85
 at ServiceStack.Redis.RedisNativeClient.SendExpectData(...)
 at ServiceStack.Redis.RedisNativeClient.GetBytes(String key)
```

Connection counts and memory appear to be well within limits. What is causing the periodic connection drops?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: Redis RDB snapshot persistence (the save directives) periodically forks the process to write the dataset to disk. With a large dataset on a modest VM, the fork stalls Redis so it stops serving clients for a period. That stall surfaces on the clients as bursts of forcibly closed connections. Fix: Disable RDB persistence by removing or turning off the save directives, so Redis no longer forks for snapshots. If persistence is needed, use AOF instead, since its rewrite frequency can be tuned.
solution: (1) The bursts correlate with RDB background saves triggered by the save directives (2) fork() for the RDB snapshot can block Redis from serving clients for milliseconds up to about a second with a large dataset (3) The issue is not connection pool or maxclients exhaustion (4) Turning off RDB persistence (or switching to tuned AOF) eliminates the drops

grounding.title: Redis IOException: "Existing connection forcibly closed by remote host" using ServiceStack C# client

question:
We run a single Elasticsearch 1.5.2 node that backs an internal search tool. Some search requests fail right away. From our Python service, using the Requests library, they show up as timeouts. When we replay the same query with curl, it returns `curl: (52) Empty reply from server` and no JSON error body at all. It only happens when the query matches a lot of documents and the response would be large. A similar query with tighter filters, so fewer hits come back, returns normally and quickly. No error code or message is returned to the client in the failing case. We haven't changed the cluster configuration. What is going on, and how can we get these larger queries to work?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: Elasticsearch runs out of memory when building the large result set. It cannot hold all the returned documents (with their _source) in memory, so it drops the connection without returning an explicit error. Fix: Add more memory, or shrink the response. Options: set "_source": false and fetch the documents separately, use source filtering to return only the fields you need, or split the query into several smaller sub-queries.
solution: (1) Failure is memory exhaustion in Elasticsearch caused by the large response size (2) No explicit error code is returned; the symptom is an empty reply or timeout (3) Reduce the payload with _source: false or source filtering, or split the query (4) Alternatively, give Elasticsearch more memory

grounding.title: "curl: (52) Empty reply from server" / timeout when querying ElastiscSearch

question:
A developer on a Linux box with Python 2.7 installed the elasticsearch Python package via pip and ran the client library's sample script unchanged. The script builds the client with `es = Elasticsearch()` and no arguments. It then indexes a small doc into 'test-index' with doc_type 'tweet', id=1, reads it back, refreshes the index and runs a match_all search.

The script fails on the first call, `es.index(...)`, with this traceback ending:

```
File "/usr/local/lib/python2.7/dist-packages/elasticsearch/connection/http_urllib3.py", line 105, in perform_request
 raise ConnectionError('N/A', str(e), e)
elasticsearch.exceptions.ConnectionError: ConnectionError(<urllib3.connection.HTTPConnection object at 0x7f0be9c14890>: Failed to establish a new connection: [Errno 111] Connection refused) caused by: NewConnectionError(...)
```

The library's documentation gives no other setup steps. The developer wants to know why the sample fails and whether something else must be configured first.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The Python package is only a client. `Elasticsearch()` with no arguments connects to an Elasticsearch server at localhost:9200 by default. No server is running there, so the TCP connection is refused. Fix: Install and start an Elasticsearch server, either locally so it listens on localhost:9200 or as a hosted instance. If it is hosted or on another port, pass that host and port to the Elasticsearch() constructor.
solution: (1) The elasticsearch Python package is a client only and needs a separate Elasticsearch server (2) Elasticsearch() with no arguments defaults to localhost port 9200 (3) Errno 111 Connection refused means nothing is listening on that host and port (4) Installing and running an Elasticsearch server on localhost:9200 fixes it

grounding.title: 'Connection refused' error trying to follow the Python Elasticsearch example usage

question:
On a macOS dev machine, PostgreSQL was installed through Homebrew, and `brew info postgres` reports 9.4.4. Connections used to work. The only recent change the user remembers is installing PHP 5.5. Now the server will not start:

```
$ postgres -D /usr/local/var/postgres
LOG: unrecognized configuration parameter "dynamic_shared_memory_type" in file "/usr/local/var/postgres/postgresql.conf" line 130
FATAL: configuration file "/usr/local/var/postgres/postgresql.conf" contains errors
```

The server log shows the same error. Line 130 of postgresql.conf is `dynamic_shared_memory_type = posix`, followed by the stock comment block. As a test, the operator commented out that line and tried again. Startup then failed with:

```
FATAL: database files are incompatible with server
DETAIL: The data directory was initialized by PostgreSQL version 9.4, which is not compatible with this version 9.3.5.
```

This is confusing because Homebrew still says 9.4.4 is installed. What is going on?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: Running `postgres` by bare name runs whichever postgres binary comes first in $PATH. On this machine that is an older PostgreSQL 9.3.5 left by a previous or different installer, not the Homebrew 9.4.4 binary. Version 9.3.5 does not know the 9.4 `dynamic_shared_memory_type` parameter and cannot open a 9.4 data directory. Fix: Run `which postgres` to find the conflicting binary. Start the Homebrew server by its absolute path, e.g. `/usr/local/bin/postgres -D /usr/local/var/postgres`; you can confirm the version with `/usr/local/bin/postgres -V`. Alternatively, fix $PATH or remove the old install.
solution: (1) A different postgres binary (9.3.5) earlier in $PATH is being run instead of Homebrew's 9.4.4 (2) `dynamic_shared_memory_type` is a 9.4 parameter unknown to 9.3 (3) Data directories are not compatible across major versions, so commenting out the config line cannot fix it (4) Use `which postgres` and start with the absolute path /usr/local/bin/postgres

grounding.title: Unrecognized configuration parameter "dynamic_shared_memory_type"

question:
We run scheduled batch collectors on GKE (1.10.9-gke.5). Each one is created with something like:

kubectl run collector-60053 --schedule="30 10 * * * *" --image=gcr.io/myimage/collector --restart=OnFailure --command node collector.js

The collectors sometimes fail, and we expected failed runs to be retried. What we see instead: the job object exists and shows 0 successful completions, but its pods are gone entirely. We have no logs to inspect, and nothing is retrying.

$ kubectl get jobs | grep 60053
collector-60053-1546943400   1   0   1h
$ kubectl get pods -a | grep 60053
(no output)

The cluster has node autoscaling enabled. While watching closely, I saw failing pods go into CrashLoopBackOff, and later a node was scaled down and the pods and their metadata vanished with it. My guess is that the autoscaler doesn't treat crash-looping pods as active workload. Either way, retried runs and their failed pods are not being kept around for inspection. Why are the failed job pods disappearing instead of being retried and retained?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The Jobs run with restartPolicy OnFailure, which has known problems in Kubernetes (issue 54870). With this policy, failed job pods are not reliably retried or kept around. They end up removed, so their logs are lost and retries stop. Fix: Change the job's restart policy to Never and set a backoffLimit on the Job. The Job controller will then create new pods for retries, up to the backoffLimit, and keep the failed pods so their logs can be inspected.
solution: (1) The problem stems from using restartPolicy OnFailure for the Job (a known Kubernetes Jobs issue). (2) With OnFailure, failed pods are not retained, so logs are lost and retries do not happen as expected. (3) Use restartPolicy Never together with a backoffLimit on the Job. (4) With Never, the Job controller retries by creating new pods up to backoffLimit and keeps the errored pods for inspection.

grounding.title: Kubernetes pods disappear after failed jobs

question:
We deploy a Kafka Streams service in a container built from openjdk:8-alpine. Stateless parts of the topology run fine. Once records reach a windowed/session aggregation, the stream thread dies during the commit/flush of the session store with:

Exception in thread "app-...-StreamThread-1" java.lang.UnsatisfiedLinkError: /tmp/librocksdbjni94709417646402513.so: Error loading shared library ld-linux-x86-64.so.2: No such file or directory (needed by /tmp/librocksdbjni94709417646402513.so)
  at org.rocksdb.NativeLibraryLoader.loadLibraryFromJar(...)
  at org.rocksdb.RocksDB.loadLibrary(...)
  at org.apache.kafka.streams.state.internals.RocksDBStore.openDB(...)
  at org.apache.kafka.streams.state.internals.RocksDBSessionStore.put(...)
  ...
  at org.apache.kafka.streams.processor.internals.StreamTask.commit(...)

The same jar works when run locally outside the container. What is causing the crash, and how should the image be changed?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The RocksDB JNI native library bundled with Kafka Streams is linked against glibc and needs the glibc loader ld-linux-x86-64.so.2. The openjdk:8-alpine image is musl-based and does not provide it, so loading the library fails as soon as a RocksDB state store is opened. Fix: Switch the base image to a glibc-compatible JDK image, such as adoptopenjdk/openjdk8:alpine-slim, so the RocksDB native library can load.
solution: (1) The RocksDB state store used for windowing loads a native JNI .so library (2) That .so depends on glibc (ld-linux-x86-64.so.2) (3) openjdk:8-alpine uses musl libc and lacks the glibc loader (4) Use a glibc-compatible base image, e.g. adoptopenjdk/openjdk8:alpine-slim
technology: Kafka Streams / RocksDB on Docker Alpine

grounding.title: Alternative to openjdk:8-alpine for Kafka Streams

question:
We run a Java web app on Tomcat inside a Docker container. Tomcat's PersistentManager with JDBCStore is supposed to write session data to a PostgreSQL database on the developer's own machine. Session persistence fails with:

SEVERE: A SQL exception occurred org.postgresql.util.PSQLException: Connection to localhost:5432 refused. Check that the hostname and port are correct and that the postmaster is accepting TCP/IP connections.

The Store element in context.xml uses connectionURL="jdbc:postgresql://localhost/admin?stringtype=unspecified" with user/password admin/admin. On the machine itself, netstat -aln | grep LISTEN shows Postgres listening on 127.0.0.1.5432 (tcp4) and ::1.5432 (tcp6). postgresql.conf has listen_addresses = localhost and port = 5432, which matches the server definition in pgAdmin3, and pgAdmin connects without problems. The container was started with default Docker settings. The operator wonders whether Docker running in a VM is relevant. They are not sure what else to check.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The container uses Docker's default bridge network, so 'localhost' inside the container resolves to the container itself rather than the machine running PostgreSQL. Nothing listens on port 5432 inside the container, so the connection is refused. Fix: Run the container with --net=host so localhost refers to the host. Alternatively, point the JDBC URL at the Docker host/gateway IP, for example by using an alias in connectionURL mapped via --add-host DB_ALIAS:<gateway-ip>, or by editing the container's /etc/hosts.
solution: (1) Default Docker network is bridge, giving the container its own network namespace (2) localhost inside the container points to the container, not the host machine (3) Postgres is not listening on 5432 inside the container, hence connection refused (4) Fix by using --net=host or by connecting to the docker host/gateway IP (e.g. via --add-host alias)

grounding.title: Using Docker to launch web app, can't connect to Postgresql DB?

question:
We run a GKE cluster with private nodes enabled. A restricted list of authorized master networks covers our office ranges, and kubectl from those locations works fine. We added a Google Cloud Build pipeline that builds a Docker image and then runs a deploy step against the cluster. The image build succeeds, but the deploy step fails with:

Unable to connect to the server: dial tcp xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx:443: i/o timeout

As a test, we temporarily added 0.0.0.0/0 to the authorized master networks and re-ran the same Cloud Build job. The build and the deploy to GKE then both completed successfully. Leaving the control plane open to the whole internet is not acceptable. We tried to find a specific range to authorize for the pipeline instead, but none of our current entries allow it. Why does the deploy only work when the endpoint is fully open, and how should this be set up properly?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: Cloud Build worker machines run outside the cluster's VPC and Google does not publish their IP ranges. Because of that, they cannot be added to the GKE master authorized networks, and their connections to the private cluster's control-plane endpoint are blocked. Fix: Keep the master authorized networks restricted, and route the Cloud Build deploy step through an SSH bastion or proxy instance on GCE inside the cluster's VPC, whose address is authorized to reach the master. Do not open the control plane to 0.0.0.0/0.
solution: (1) Cloud Build build machines cannot be attached to or placed inside the customer VPC (2) Cloud Build does not announce or publish fixed IP ranges for its workers, so they cannot be allowlisted in master authorized networks (3) The i/o timeout is the master authorized networks blocking Cloud Build's source IPs (4) The workaround is a bastion/proxy GCE instance in the VPC that Cloud Build uses to reach the GKE master
technology: Google Kubernetes Engine private clusters / Google Cloud Build

grounding.title: Google Cloud Build deploy to GKE Private Cluster

question:
After routine plugin updates on our Jenkins controller, every pipeline that runs on Kubernetes agents fails. The updates included Kubernetes Client API, which went to 1.30.3; we also tried 1.31.1 and got the same result. As soon as a build starts, the Jenkins log repeats this:

```
Timer task org.csanchez.jenkins.plugins.kubernetes.KubernetesClientProvider$UpdateConnectionCount@2c16d367 failed
java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: 'okhttp3.OkHttpClient io.fabric8.kubernetes.client.HttpClientAware.getHttpClient()'
 at org.csanchez.jenkins.plugins.kubernetes.KubernetesClientProvider$UpdateConnectionCount.doRun(KubernetesClientProvider.java:150)
 at hudson.triggers.SafeTimerTask.run(SafeTimerTask.java:90)
 ...
```

After several of these, the build is aborted while launching a shell step inside the pod container:

```
java.io.IOException: Timed out waiting for websocket connection. You should increase the value of system property org.csanchez.jenkins.plugins.kubernetes.pipeline.ContainerExecDecorator.websocketConnectionTimeout currently set at 30 seconds
 at org.csanchez.jenkins.plugins.kubernetes.pipeline.ContainerExecDecorator$1.doLaunch(ContainerExecDecorator.java:451)
```

Before these updates, builds on the same cluster worked fine. Why are they failing now, and how do we fix it?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The newer kubernetes-client-api plugin (fabric8 client) changed or removed the HttpClientAware.getHttpClient() method returning okhttp3.OkHttpClient. The installed Kubernetes plugin still calls that method, so the two plugin versions are binary-incompatible. Fix: Downgrade the Kubernetes Client API plugin to kubernetes-client-api:5.10.1-171.vaa0774fb8c20. Alternatively, upgrade the Kubernetes plugin to 1.31.2, which is compatible with the new client library (JENKINS-67483).
solution: (1) The NoSuchMethodError indicates a binary incompatibility between the Kubernetes plugin and the updated kubernetes-client-api (fabric8) library. (2) The websocket timeout is a downstream symptom, not a reason to raise the timeout. (3) Fix by downgrading kubernetes-client-api to 5.10.1-171.vaa0774fb8c20 or upgrading the Kubernetes plugin to 1.31.2.

grounding.title: Jenkins with Kubernetes Client Plugin - NoSuchMethodError

question:
We run a Linux container-based Azure Function on an ElasticPremium EP1 App Service Plan. Both are managed in Terraform with azurerm provider ~>2.24.0. The plan is defined with kind = "FunctionApp", reserved = true and sku tier ElasticPremium/EP1. The function_app references the plan's id and has an explicit depends_on on the plan.

The function runs fine. However, every terraform apply now fails, even for unrelated changes:

Error deleting App Service Plan "asp-staging" ... StatusCode=409 -- Conflict: Server farm 'asp-staging' cannot be deleted because it has web app(s) function-staging assigned to it. (ExtendedCode 11003)

Another plan in the same setup hosts a regular App Service and applies without problems. I tried removing every reference to the function and its plan from the config, and the same error appeared. Adding depends_on, as suggested by the provider maintainers, did not help either.

If I delete the function and the plan in the portal, the next apply succeeds once and recreates them. After that, applies fail again. Why does Terraform keep trying to delete this plan?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: Azure stores the Elastic Premium plan's kind as "elastic" rather than the configured "FunctionApp". On every plan, Terraform sees a diff on kind, which forces replacement (destroy/recreate) of the App Service Plan. The delete fails with a 409 because the function app is still attached. Fix: Change the azurerm_app_service_plan kind attribute to "elastic" so it matches what Azure reports. Terraform then stops planning a replacement of the service plan on each apply.
solution: (1) terraform plan shows the app service plan 'must be replaced' on each apply (2) kind drifts from "FunctionApp" to "elastic" for ElasticPremium plans and the kind change forces replacement (3) the 409 occurs because Terraform tries to delete the plan while the function app is still assigned to it (4) set kind = "elastic" in config to stop the replacement
technology: Terraform azurerm provider / Azure App Service Plan (Elastic Premium Functions)

grounding.title: Terraform Error deleting App Service Plan StatusCode=409 Server farm [asp] cannot be deleted because it has web app(s) [azure-function] assigned to it

question:
Our Jenkins controller uses the Kubernetes plugin to launch build agents as pods in an Amazon EKS cluster running Kubernetes 1.12.x. Around 8:45 PM EST on Aug 29, 2019, agent provisioning began failing. Nobody changed anything on our side; I'm the only admin. Rebooting the EKS worker node and the Jenkins controller didn't help. kubectl works and shows one Ready node.

Jenkins log at the time:

```
INFO: Started provisioning Kubernetes Pod Template from eks with 1 executors.
INFO: Created Pod: jenkins-eks-39hfp in namespace jenkins
INFO: ALPN callback dropped: HTTP/2 is disabled. Is alpn-boot on the boot class path?
WARNING: Exec Failure: HTTP 403, Status: 403 -
java.net.ProtocolException: Expected HTTP 101 response but was '403 Forbidden'
 at okhttp3.internal.ws.RealWebSocket.checkResponse(RealWebSocket.java:229)
 ...
WARNING: Error in provisioning; agent=KubernetesSlave name: jenkins-eks-39hfp, template=PodTemplate{... namespace='jenkins' ... volumes=[HostPathVolume /var/run/docker.sock ...]}
```

The ALPN/HTTP/2 messages never appeared in our logs before this started. That makes me wonder whether something changed on the AWS side.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: AWS pushed a patch to EKS Kubernetes 1.12.x control planes for the Go net/http CVE. The patched API server rejects the websocket exec/watch upgrade from the older Jenkins Kubernetes plugin with 403 instead of 101. The ALPN messages are a red herring. Fix: Upgrade the Jenkins Kubernetes plugin to version 1.18.3 or later, which is compatible with the patched API server (JENKINS-59000).
solution: (1) The change was on the AWS side: EKS 1.12.x control planes got a Go net/http CVE security patch. (2) The older Kubernetes plugin version is incompatible with the patched API server, so the websocket exec upgrade gets 403 instead of 101. (3) The ALPN/HTTP/2 info messages are not the cause. (4) The fix is upgrading the Kubernetes plugin to 1.18.3 or later.
technology: Jenkins Kubernetes plugin on Amazon EKS

grounding.title: Jenkins suddenly started failing to provision agents in Amazon EKS

question:
On an Ubuntu 16.04.4 host (kernel 4.13.0-43) we're running a Docker daemon built from source (Server Version: dev). Any `docker pull` fails with:

Error response from daemon: Get https://registry-1.docker.io/v2/: proxyconnect tcp: tls: oversized record received with length 20527

The corporate proxy is configured for the daemon through a systemd drop-in under /etc/systemd/system/docker.service.d/, following the standard docs. `docker info` shows both HTTP Proxy and HTTPS Proxy set. registry-1.docker.io is also listed under Insecure Registries. The previously packaged daemon on this machine pulled fine through the same proxy settings. A colleague hit the same error right after a yum update moved them from Docker 17.09 to 18.06. Switching DNS to 8.8.8.8 made no difference. `ping registry-1.docker.io` shows 100% packet loss, though ICMP is probably blocked here anyway. Need to know why the pull fails and how to fix it.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The HTTPS_PROXY variable in the daemon's systemd proxy drop-in uses an https:// URL (https://user:pwd@proxy:port). Newer Docker versions honour that scheme and attempt a TLS handshake with the proxy itself. The proxy only speaks plain HTTP, so its response is parsed as an invalid, oversized TLS record. Fix: Edit /etc/systemd/system/docker.service.d/https-proxy.conf so the proxy URL uses the http scheme: HTTPS_PROXY=http://user:pwd@proxy:port. Then run `systemctl daemon-reload` and restart docker.
solution: (1) The error comes from the daemon's connection to the proxy (proxyconnect), not from the registry. (2) HTTPS_PROXY is set with an https:// scheme, so the daemon tries TLS to the proxy. (3) The proxy speaks plain HTTP, which produces the 'oversized record' TLS error. (4) Change HTTPS_PROXY to http://... and restart the daemon; older Docker versions tolerated the https:// scheme.

grounding.title: Ubuntu, Docker - proxyconnect tcp: tls: oversized record received with length 20527

question:
After running apt-get update && apt-get upgrade on an Ubuntu host (later upgraded 18.04 -> 20.04), hourly cron jobs of the form `0 * * * * cd /project/folder && docker-compose run --rm service_name` stopped completing. `top` shows the processes piling up every hour, and the container's command never actually starts. Versions now: Docker 20.10.4 (build d3cb89e), docker-compose 1.28.4, containerd 1.4.3, runc 1.0.0-rc92, kernel 5.4.0-66. Reinstalling docker and docker-compose from the official repo and rebooting changed nothing. Reduced to a trivial compose file (alpine image, command `ash -c "date"`) and it still hangs under cron. Adding `--verbose` and redirecting to a log shows compose stalling right after it invokes `/usr/bin/docker start --attach --interactive`. Running the exact same command line, including the redirect to the log file, from an interactive terminal works fine and exits normally.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: A regression in Docker Engine/CLI 20.10.4 causes `docker start --attach --interactive` (which docker-compose run shells out to) to hang when there is no TTY, as under cron. Earlier/later Docker versions don't have the bug. Fix: Upgrade Docker to 20.10.5 (where the bug is fixed) or downgrade to 20.10.3. As a short-term workaround, set COMPOSE_INTERACTIVE_NO_CLI=1 in the crontab so docker-compose doesn't shell out to the docker CLI for the interactive attach.
solution: (1) Bug is specific to Docker 20.10.4 picked up by the apt upgrade (2) Hang occurs in docker start --attach --interactive when run without a terminal (cron) (3) Fix by upgrading to 20.10.5 or downgrading to 20.10.3 (4) Workaround: COMPOSE_INTERACTIVE_NO_CLI=1 in the cron environment

grounding.title: Running "docker-compose run" hangs when it's run in cron

question:
I'm new to GeoDjango and am trying to store a longitude/latitude point in a PostgreSQL/PostGIS table. The model has this field:

    geolocation = models.PointField(_('Geo Location'), geography=True, null=True, blank=True, help_text=_('Geolocation with Longitude and Latitude'))
    objects = models.GeoManager()

In the view, before saving the form, I set:

    savedProject.geolocation = GEOSGeometry('POINT(%s %s)' % (u_lng, u_lat))

When the form is submitted and saved, Django raises:

    Exception Type: InternalError
    Exception Value: current transaction is aborted, commands ignored until end of transaction block

The Django error page gives only this generic InternalError and does not show which SQL caused it. I suspect a bad SQL statement somewhere, but I don't know which one. What is actually going on, and how do I find the statement at fault?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The 'current transaction is aborted' error is not the real failure. An earlier SQL statement in the same PostgreSQL transaction failed. After that, PostgreSQL rejects every later command in the transaction, so the statement Django reports is just the next one that got rejected. Fix: Turn on Django SQL logging: add a LOGGING config with the 'django' logger at DEBUG level sent to a console handler, and set DEBUG=True. Then rerun runserver and reproduce the save so all queries print to the console. Run the last logged queries one by one in a database client such as psql to find the one that fails, then fix that query.
solution: (1) The reported error is a symptom; a previous SQL statement in the same transaction failed first (2) PostgreSQL ignores all further commands in a transaction after one statement errors, until the transaction ends (3) Enable Django SQL logging (django logger at DEBUG, DEBUG=True) to see the executed queries (4) Run the logged queries directly against the database to find the one that actually fails

grounding.title: How to debug: Internal Error current transaction is aborted, commands ignored until end of transaction block

question:
A developer on Windows runs an ASP.NET Core project with Visual Studio 2017 Docker tooling, using Linux containers. The project compiles, but launching it with F5 or the Docker run button fails in the PrepareForLaunch MSBuild task:

```
Creating network "dockercompose1627893588_default" with the default driver
Building pswebapi
Service 'pswebapi' failed to build: Get https://registry-1.docker.io/v2/microsoft/aspnetcore/manifests/1.1: unauthorized: incorrect username or password
```

The Dockerfile is minimal:
```
FROM microsoft/aspnetcore:1.1
ARG source
WORKDIR /app
EXPOSE 80
COPY ${source:-obj/Docker/publish} .
ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "PsWebApi.dll"]
```

The C: drive is shared in Docker settings. All NuGet packages have been updated to the latest versions, and the error persists. The developer had previously signed in to Docker Hub on this machine.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: Docker was logged in to Docker Hub using the account's email address instead of the Docker ID (username). Registry pulls of the base image are rejected with 'incorrect username or password' as a result. Fix: Run `docker logout`, then run `docker login` and enter the Docker ID username, not the email address. The ID is shown on the Docker Hub site after signing in with the email.
solution: (1) The error comes from authenticating to registry-1.docker.io while pulling the base image, not from the project build itself. (2) The stored login used the email address rather than the Docker ID/username. (3) Fix by running docker logout, then docker login with the Docker ID.
technology: Docker / Docker Hub with Visual Studio ASP.NET Core tooling

grounding.title: failed to build: Get https://registry-1.docker.io/v2/microsoft/aspnetcore/manifests/1.1: unauthorized: incorrect username or password

question:
I'm running a Flask API, a React client, a dev SMTP container and Postgres 13-alpine with docker-compose. Earlier I had trouble with the Postgres password and with the entry.sh file not being found, so I updated Docker. Since the update, `docker-compose up` crashes with a Go panic:

```
panic: runtime error: index out of range [1] with length 1
goroutine 37 [running]:
github.com/docker/compose-cli/pkg/compose.(*convergence).ensureService(...)
 github.com/docker/compose-cli/pkg/compose/convergence.go:222 +0x11f1
github.com/docker/compose-cli/pkg/compose.(*convergence).apply.func1(...)
 convergence.go:99
```

Compose file details:
- Every service sets `container_name` (api, client, email).
- The `api` service publishes 5000:5000, uses env_file ./api/.env, depends_on db, and runs gunicorn.
- The `email` service builds from the same Dockerfile and image name (mutcompute-api) and publishes 8025.
- `db` publishes 5405:5432 and has restart: always.

Sometimes, after I edit the compose file, the output shows it starting to recreate containers and then panicking:

```
⠙ Container api Recreate 0.2s
⠙ Container bb72362b9e19_api Recreate 0.2s
panic: runtime error: index out of range [1] with length 1
```

The React client was working before the update. I don't know what the Go panic means or why it happens.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: Containers from previous compose runs were still around in the background, including a stale hash-prefixed `bb72362b9e19_api`. They kept host ports such as 5000 bound. Compose's convergence logic panicked on these leftovers instead of reporting the real error, which was 'Bind for 0.0.0.0:5000 failed: port is already allocated'. Fix: Tear down the existing project containers with `docker-compose down`, optionally running `docker-compose up --remove-orphans` first. Then run `docker-compose up` again.
solution: (1) Stale or orphan containers from earlier runs still exist (e.g. bb72362b9e19_api) (2) Those leftover containers hold host ports (port 5000 already allocated) (3) The Go panic in convergence.go hides the underlying port/container conflict (4) Running docker-compose down (and/or --remove-orphans) before up resolves it

grounding.title: Docker-compose error -- panic: runtime error: index out of range [1] with length 1

question:
Our Rails app runs on Heroku with PostgreSQL. In production, latency spikes show up about once an hour. APM traces for the slow requests all show the same query, executed around 100 times within a single HTTP request and adding up to more than 1.5 seconds:

```
SELECT a.attname, format_type(a.atttypid, a.atttypmod), pg_get_expr(d.adbin, d.adrelid), a.attnotnull, a.atttypid, a.atttypmod FROM pg_attribute a
LEFT JOIN pg_attrdef d ON a.attrelid = d.adrelid AND a.attnum = d.adnum
WHERE a.attrelid = ?::regclass AND a.attnum > ? AND NOT a.attisdropped
ORDER BY a.attnum
```

None of our code queries pg_attribute directly. It looks like Rails issues this to work out model attributes. We expected Rails to do this once and reuse the result, so we don't understand why it keeps happening on a schedule. We need to know why it recurs and how to get rid of the cost.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: Rails runs this column-introspection query once per table/model in each newly started process, not once per request. The hourly spikes mean the app processes are being restarted regularly, and every fresh process has to introspect the schema again on its first requests. Fix: Find out why the processes restart so often. To remove the runtime queries completely, generate a schema cache with `RAILS_ENV=production rails db:schema:cache:dump` (Rails 4: `bin/rake db:schema:cache:dump`). New processes then load that file instead of querying the database. Regenerate the cache after every schema change.
solution: (1) Rails introspects columns via pg_attribute once per table per process, not per request (2) Recurring spikes indicate processes are being restarted frequently (cold processes re-query) (3) Use db:schema:cache:dump so processes load the schema from a cache file (4) The schema cache must be regenerated after schema migrations

grounding.title: How to fix a slow implicit query on pg_attribute table in Rails

question:
We deployed oauth2-proxy and put a Service in front of it. The Service listens on port 80 and targets container port 4180, and we've checked the port and targetPort mapping more than once. The endpoints object looks correct:

```
$ kubectl get endpoints
NAME           ENDPOINTS           AGE
kubernetes     10.40.63.79:443     82d
oauth2-proxy   10.40.34.212:4180   33s
```

From another pod in the same namespace, a direct curl fails:

```
# curl 10.40.34.212:4180
curl: (7) Failed to connect to 10.40.34.212 port 4180: Connection refused
```

Curling the Service name fails the same way.

If we run `kubectl port-forward oauth2-proxy-559dd9ddf4-8z72c 4180:4180` and then curl localhost:4180, we get the expected HTTP 403 page back from oauth2-proxy.

We also confirmed that the Service selector (app.kubernetes.io/name=oauth2-proxy, app.kubernetes.io/part-of=oauth2-proxy) matches the pod. That pod is 1/1 Running with 0 restarts.

Why is the endpoint refusing connections when port-forward works?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: oauth2-proxy by default binds its HTTP listener to 127.0.0.1:4180 (loopback only) inside the container, so connections arriving on the pod IP are refused, while kubectl port-forward connects via the pod's localhost and succeeds. Fix: Configure oauth2-proxy to listen on all interfaces by adding the argument -http-address=0.0.0.0:4180 to the container.
solution: (1) The process is listening on 127.0.0.1:4180, not 0.0.0.0 (visible via netstat inside the container) (2) port-forward reaches the container's localhost, which is why it works while pod IP/Service traffic is refused (3) Fix is setting -http-address=0.0.0.0:4180 so the app binds all interfaces

grounding.title: Kubernetes: connection refused on the endpoint of a working pod

question:
Workstation running Ubuntu 18.04.1 (kernel 4.15.0-32). Docker was upgraded to 'Docker version 18.09.0-ce-tp5, build 9eb3d36'. Before the upgrade our docker-compose stack worked fine. Now `docker-compose up` fails:

ERROR: for mysql_1 Cannot start service mysql: OCI runtime create failed: unable to retrieve OCI runtime error (open /run/containerd/io.containerd.runtime.v1.linux/moby/2427.../log.json: no such file or directory): exec: "docker-runc": executable file not found in $PATH: unknown

Relevant `docker info` output:
- Server Version: 18.09.0-ce-tp5, storage driver aufs, cgroupfs
- Runtimes: containerd runc
- Default Runtime: containerd
- containerd version: ce243288... (expected: 468a545b...)
- runc version: 1555a789... (expected: 69663f0b...)
- Product License: Community Engine

The daemon itself starts, and it reports 14 containers. New containers fail to start with the error above. What is going on and how do we get back to a working state?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The installed Docker 18.09.0-ce-tp5 is a pre-beta technical preview build. It contains major, still-unstable changes to the containerd integration, so it breaks container creation: it looks for a docker-runc binary that is not present, and the containerd/runc versions do not match what it expects. Fix: Move off the tp5 preview build. Either downgrade to the stable Docker 18.06.1 release, or upgrade to the newer 18.09 beta1 release.
solution: (1) The version '18.09.0-ce-tp5' is a technical preview / pre-beta release, not a stable release. (2) The preview build carries large containerd integration changes that cause the OCI runtime / docker-runc failure. (3) The mismatched containerd and runc versions ('expected' differs from the actual) point to a broken pre-release install. (4) The remedy is to downgrade to stable 18.06.1 or move to 18.09 beta1.

grounding.title: exec: "docker-runc": executable file not found in $PATH: unknown

question:
I'm setting up Elasticsearch, with the mapper-attachments plugin installed, to index a large batch of PDFs. So far I can't get even one document in. Following the attachment tutorial, I build a JSON file that holds the PDF as base64:

coded=`cat fn6742.pdf | perl -MMIME::Base64 -ne 'print encode_base64($_)'`
json="{\"file\":\"${coded}\"}"
echo "$json" > json.file

I also tried encoding with `openssl base64 -in fn6742.pdf` and got the same result. The file starts with {"file":"JVBERi0xLjQNJeLjz9MNCjE1OCAw..., which looks right to me.

Then I submit it:

$ curl -X POST "localhost:9200/test/attachment/" -d json.file
{"error":"ElasticSearchParseException[Failed to derive xcontent from (offset=0, length=9): [106, 115, 111, 110, 46, 102, 105, 108, 101]]","status":400}

The server log at DEBUG shows: Failed to execute [index {[test][attachment][DauMB-vtTIaYGyKD4P8Y_w], source[json.file]}] with the same ElasticSearchParseException raised from XContentFactory.xContent / DocumentMapper.parse.

I can't tell whether the JSON is malformed or the PDF/attachment setup is broken.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The curl command sent the literal 9-character string "json.file" as the request body instead of the file's contents. The byte values in the error decode to 'j','s','o','n','.','f','i','l','e', which is not valid JSON, so Elasticsearch could not parse it. Fix: Prefix the filename with @ so curl reads the request body from the file: curl -X POST "localhost:9200/test/attachment/" -d @json.file
solution: (1) The bytes in the error [106,115,...,101] are the UTF-8 codes for the string "json.file". (2) curl's -d option without @ sends its argument literally as the request body. (3) Neither the base64 encoding nor the attachment plugin is at fault. (4) Use -d @json.file so curl sends the file's contents.

grounding.title: Elasticsearch Parse Exception error when attempting to index PDF

question:
We run Tomcat 9 inside a Docker container and attach IntelliJ (running on the Docker host) for remote debugging. Container port 49540 is published to host port 49540. Tomcat is started with CATALINA_OPTS containing JMX settings (port 49520, java.rmi.server.hostname=10.0.75.1) plus:

-agentlib:jdwp=transport=dt_socket,address=49540,suspend=n,server=y

On the openjdk:8-slim base image this worked fine: IntelliJ attaches, and `telnet localhost 49540` from the host connects. After switching the base image to openjdk:9-slim, nothing else changed, and the host can no longer reach the debug port. IntelliJ reports SocketTimeoutException: Connection reset. Running telnet to the debug port from inside the container still connects. We tried several other Java 9 images (other openjdk tags, adenix/java) and got the same result.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: Starting with JDK 9, the JDWP agent binds to localhost only when the address has just a port and no host. The debugger therefore listens only on the container's loopback interface, so connections forwarded from the Docker host through the published port are refused or reset. Fix: Tell JDWP to listen on all interfaces by using a wildcard host in the address, e.g. JPDA_OPTS="-agentlib:jdwp=transport=dt_socket,address=*:49540,server=y,suspend=n". Then start Tomcat with `catalina.sh jpda run`.
solution: (1) JDK 9 changed the JDWP default so a port-only address binds to localhost/loopback (2) Inside the container the port is reachable, but traffic forwarded through Docker port mapping is not (3) Use address=*:49540 to bind on all interfaces (e.g. via JPDA_OPTS with catalina.sh jpda run)
technology: Java 9 / Tomcat 9 / Docker JDWP remote debugging

grounding.title: Can't remotely debug on Java 9 Tomcat 9 in docker container

question:
Installing a Helm (v2, Tiller tunnel) chart fails with: `Error: found in requirements.yaml, but missing in charts/ directory: dependency-chart`.

requirements.yaml:
```
dependencies:
- name: dependency-chart
  repository: "@some-repo"
  version: 0.1.0
```
Steps run:
```
rm -rf charts
helm dep up
helm upgrade --install chart-to-install . --debug
```
`helm dep up` reports success: it updates the some-repo repo (gs://some-repo), prints "Saving 1 charts", downloads dependency-chart and deletes outdated charts. After that, `ls charts/` shows dependency-chart-0.1.0.tgz. The install still fails with the error above right after the debug tunnel is created.

Several other charts depend on the same dependency-chart and install fine. `helm lint` reports that the directory name (helm) does not match the chart name, recommends an icon, and warns that templates/ was not found. The other, working charts show the same lint error, so it doesn't seem relevant. Changing the requirement to point at a local copy of the chart instead of the repo alias gives the same error. What is causing Helm to not see the dependency?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The chart's .helmignore file contains an entry for charts/. When Helm loads the chart it skips everything .helmignore matches, so the downloaded dependency tarball in charts/ is ignored. Helm then treats the dependency as missing. Fix: Remove the charts/ entry from .helmignore, then re-run helm dep up and the install.
solution: (1) Helm skips any file matched by .helmignore when it loads the chart (2) charts/ is listed in .helmignore (3) Because of this, the dependency tgz is present on disk but not loaded (4) Removing charts/ from .helmignore fixes the error

grounding.title: Error: found in requirements.yaml, but missing in charts/ directory: dependency-chart

question:
Our Elasticsearch node has 16 GB of memory. We recently started running aggregations against a syslog index and one query brings the node down with "java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space". The query filters with a query_string on DstCountry:CN, then runs a terms aggregation on SrcIP, a nested terms aggregation on DstIP under it, and a terms aggregation on DstPort under that:

POST /test-index-syslog3/type-syslog/_search
{ "query": { "query_string": { "default_field": "DstCountry", "query": "CN" } },
  "aggs": { "whatever": { "terms": { "field": "SrcIP" },
    "aggs": { "destination_ip": { "terms": { "field": "DstIP" },
      "aggs": { "port": { "terms": { "field": "DstPort" } } } } } } } }

Running only the query part returns 1266 hits, so the matching set is small and we can't see why memory is exhausted. The index itself holds far more syslog documents than that. We'd like to know whether the aggregation is built wrong or what is actually consuming the heap.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: To aggregate, Elasticsearch un-inverts the entire SrcIP, DstIP and DstPort fields across the whole index into in-heap fielddata so it can look up values by document ID, regardless of how few documents the query matches. Loading these full fields exhausts the Java heap. Fix: Map the aggregated fields with doc_values so per-document values are stored on disk in a column-oriented form and served via the OS filesystem cache, instead of loading entire fields into heap; reindex as needed.
solution: (1) Terms aggregations load fielddata for the whole field, not just matching hits (2) The small hit count (1266) does not limit memory used by fielddata (3) SrcIP/DstIP/DstPort fielddata on heap causes the OOM (4) Use doc_values for aggregated fields to rely on OS cache instead of heap

grounding.title: Elasticsearch query with nested aggregations causing out of memory

question:
PostgreSQL 9.6 on Windows, provisioned by a setup script: initdb, register and start the Windows service, create an empty database, restore a dump. Once the script completes, the schema and data are fine, but pg_xlog already holds 55 segment files (~880 MB). We need that directory kept small.

What we changed: wal_keep_segments set to 0 (also tried 1), max_wal_size set to 200MB, checkpoint_timeout lowered, archive_mode off, archive_command set to an empty string. Querying pg_settings shows all of these values are active.

After that we ran manual CHECKPOINTs through SQL, ran VACUUM on the database, restarted the Windows service, and tried pg_archivecleanup. pg_xlog only dropped to 50 files (~800 MB), nowhere near the 200 MB limit now configured. No errors appear. Why is the directory still this large, and how do we bring it down?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The WAL segments were created during the restore, while max_wal_size was still the default 1GB. PostgreSQL does not delete already-allocated segments right away when the limit is lowered. It only decides to delete or recycle a segment when that segment fills up and gets recycled, so the directory shrinks gradually. Fix: Wait for normal WAL activity to recycle segments, which removes the excess over the new max_wal_size. To speed it up, force several WAL switches with SELECT pg_switch_xlog() (and checkpoints) so old segments get cycled and deleted.
solution: (1) Existing segments were preallocated while max_wal_size was the default 1GB (2) Lowering max_wal_size does not immediately delete existing WAL files (3) Segments are removed or renamed for reuse only when a segment fills up and is recycled (4) Calling pg_switch_xlog() repeatedly forces recycling and shrinks pg_xlog

grounding.title: How to enable auto clean of pg_xlog

question:
Local dev cluster: Minikube v0.19.0 on macOS Sierra with the xhyve driver. The ingress addon was enabled with `minikube addons enable ingress` and is running the bundled nginx controller (0.9.0-beta.4). Test workload: `kubectl run nginx --image=nginx --port=80`, then `kubectl expose deployment nginx --target-port=80 --type=NodePort`. The service shows 80:31635/TCP.

An Ingress (extensions/v1beta1) named basic-ingress was applied. It has no annotations and only a default backend of serviceName nginx, servicePort 80. `kubectl get ingress` shows hosts *, address 192.168.64.37, port 80. `kubectl describe ingress` shows the backend resolving to 172.17.0.3:80, with CREATE/UPDATE events from the ingress controller.

When I browse to http://192.168.64.37, the browser jumps to https and fails with "secure connection failed" in both Firefox and Chrome. `curl 192.168.64.37` returns an HTML page reading "301 Moved Permanently" with the footer nginx/1.11.12. No TLS secret or certificate has been set up. The "Welcome to nginx" page never appears through the Ingress.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The nginx ingress controller redirects HTTP requests to HTTPS (port 443) by default. No TLS is configured, so every plain-HTTP request gets a 301 redirect to an HTTPS endpoint that doesn't work. Fix: Add the annotation `ingress.kubernetes.io/ssl-redirect: "false"` to the Ingress metadata and re-apply it. This turns off the forced HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect, so the backend is served over plain HTTP.
solution: (1) The 301 comes from the nginx ingress controller, not the backend nginx pod (2) The controller forces an HTTP-to-HTTPS (443) redirect by default (3) No TLS/HTTPS is configured, so the redirect target fails (4) Disable the redirect with the ingress.kubernetes.io/ssl-redirect: "false" annotation

grounding.title: Kubernetes / Minikube Ingress error (301 Moved Permanently)

question:
Ubuntu dev workstation, Docker host. A Rails app runs inside a container named 'rails' (image 'rails', started with command 'bash', Rails server launched from inside the container). Opening http://localhost:3000 in a browser gives ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED. `docker ps` shows the container up with `0.0.0.0:3000->3000/tcp`. `docker inspect rails` reports Gateway 172.17.0.1. Pinging 172.17.0.1 works. `nmap -p 3000 172.17.0.1` (Nmap 6.40) reports `3000/tcp closed`. `sudo netstat -tulpn` on the host shows docker-proxy listening on `:::3000`, along with several other docker-proxy ports (3001, 3002, 4200, 5432, 6379, 8080, etc.) for other containers. Inside the container the Rails server says it started on port 3000. Why can't the browser reach the app, and how should it be fixed?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The Rails server inside the container listens only on localhost (127.0.0.1), which is the default for newer Rails versions. Traffic forwarded by Docker into the container's network interface therefore has nothing listening to receive it, even though the port is published. Fix: Start the Rails server bound to all interfaces with `-b 0.0.0.0`. For example: `docker run -p 3000:3000 -d rails server -p 3000 -b 0.0.0.0`, or run `rails server -b 0.0.0.0` inside the container.
solution: (1) The Rails server listens only on localhost/127.0.0.1 by default in newer versions (2) Localhost inside the container is not reachable through Docker's port forwarding (3) The host-side docker-proxy and port mapping are fine; the in-container listener is the problem (4) Fix by passing -b 0.0.0.0 to rails server

grounding.title: can't access docker container

question:
After adding one more environment variable to our app's Deployment template in the Helm chart, upgrades of the release stopped working. Running `helm upgrade <release> <chart>` fails with:

```
Error: UPGRADE FAILED: The order in patch list:
[ map[name:APP_ENV value:prod] map[name:MAILER_URL value:...] map[name:APP_VERSION value:v0-0-3] map[name:APP_COMMIT_SHA value:...] ]
doesn't match $setElementOrder list:
[ map[name:APP_ENV] map[name:COMPOSER_HOME] map[name:PHP_XDEBUG_ENABLED] map[name:DATABASE_DRIVER] map[name:DATABASE_HOST] ... map[name:APP_VERSION] map[name:APP_COMMIT_SHA] map[name:APP_CRON] map[name:DATABASE_PASSWORD] map[name:MAILER_URL] ... ]
```

The container has a long `env:` list of about 20+ variables, some literal values and some pulled from secrets. The odd part is that `helm upgrade <release> <chart> --dry-run` renders and completes with no error. Only the real upgrade against the cluster fails. Previous upgrades before this env change worked fine. We need to know what is causing the patch to be rejected and how to get upgrades working again.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The Deployment's container `env` list contains the same environment variable name more than once. Env is merged by name in the strategic merge patch, so duplicate keys make the computed patch order inconsistent with the `$setElementOrder` list, and the API server rejects the patch. Fix: Find the duplicated env var entries in the chart's Deployment template and values, and remove them so each name appears only once. Then rerun `helm upgrade`.
solution: (1) The container env list has a duplicated variable name (2) Strategic merge patch merges env entries by name, so duplicates cause the $setElementOrder mismatch (3) --dry-run passes because it does not send the patch to the API server (4) Removing the duplicate entry fixes the upgrade

grounding.title: helm error when updating: UPGRADE FAILED: The order in patch list

question:
We run Helm v2.12.3 (client and server) with Tiller v2.12.3 in kube-system. The Tiller pod is Running and Ready with 0 restarts, and its env includes TILLER_NAMESPACE=kube-system and TILLER_HISTORY_MAX=0. Since yesterday we cannot install or upgrade our custom chart 'foo'. The chart has deployment, ingress and service templates and pulls from our private registry via imagePullSecret.

Running `helm install --name foo . -f values.yaml --namespace foo-namespace` returns:
`Error: release foo failed: the server could not find the requested resource`

Running `helm upgrade --install foo . -f values.yaml --namespace foo-namespace`, or a plain `helm upgrade`, returns:
`Error: UPGRADE FAILED: "foo" has no deployed releases`

We already ran `helm del --purge foo` and retried. The same errors came back. Tiller looks healthy and the versions match. What is blocking the deployment and how do we recover?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: Tiller keeps release history as ConfigMaps (labeled OWNER=TILLER) in its namespace, kube-system. A broken or failed release record for 'foo' is still there, so Helm sees a release with no successfully deployed revision and refuses to upgrade. Leftover objects from that failed release also break new installs. Fix: List the release ConfigMaps with `kubectl get cm --all-namespaces -l OWNER=TILLER` and delete the broken one for 'foo' in kube-system. Next, manually delete the release's leftover objects (deployment, service, ingress, etc.) and reinstall with Helm. If that does not work, upgrade Helm and reinstall Tiller.
solution: (1) Helm v2/Tiller stores release state as ConfigMaps in Tiller's namespace (kube-system), labeled OWNER=TILLER (2) A broken or failed release record causes the 'has no deployed releases' error (3) Delete the stale release ConfigMap(s) for foo (4) Manually remove leftover release resources (deployment/service/ingress) before reinstalling

grounding.title: Helm install or upgrade release failed on Kubernetes cluster: the server could not find the requested resource or UPGRADE FAILED: no deployed releases

question:
On a developer workstation (192.168.0.108) I'm running Elasticsearch 0.90.0 in the foreground with `bin/elasticsearch -f`. I intended this as a standalone local instance and haven't modified config/elasticsearch.yml from the shipped defaults.

Startup looks normal at first:
- "initializing ... loaded [], sites [] ... initialized ... starting"
- transport reports bound_address 0:0:0:0:0:0:0:0:9301, publish_address 192.168.0.108:9301

About six seconds later discovery.zen begins warning, and the warning keeps repeating:

```
[WARN ][discovery.zen] [Myers, Fred] failed to connect to master [[Holly][nlr9o-yfSQ6MsTtYlTlqlw][inet[/192.168.1.6:9300]]], retrying...
org.elasticsearch.transport.ConnectTransportException: [Holly][inet[/192.168.1.6:9300]] connect_timeout[30s]
...
Caused by: java.net.NoRouteToHostException: No route to host
```

The transport.netty layer also logs "exception caught on transport layer ... closing connection" with the same NoRouteToHostException.

I don't recognise the node "Holly" or the host 192.168.1.6, and I never configured either. The node never becomes usable. Why is it trying to reach that master, and how do I get it to run on its own?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
