- Providers: AWS and DigitalOcean, with various instance and disk types
- Host swap and swappiness
- Docker --memory-swap and swappiness

Some of these helped partially. Changing the memory limit or the container count always brought the failures back.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: Writes go into the kernel's page cache as dirty pages, and those pages are charged to the container's memory cgroup. When many containers compete for disk I/O, the dirty pages are not flushed fast enough. They build up until they exceed the container's memory limit, and the container is OOMKilled or allocation fails. Fix: Limit the dirty page cache with host sysctls so writeback starts before the cgroup limit is reached. Set vm.dirty_bytes no higher than the per-container memory limit, for example `sysctl -w vm.dirty_bytes=134217728` for 128M containers. Also lower vm.dirty_background_ratio, for example `sysctl -w vm.dirty_background_ratio=15`.
solution: (1) Dirty pages (the write cache) accumulate and count against the container's memory limit (2) Disk I/O contention from many concurrent writers delays flushing, so the dirty cache grows (3) Tune vm.dirty_bytes / vm.dirty_background_ratio (or the _bytes variant) via sysctl (4) vm.dirty_bytes should not exceed the container memory limit

grounding.title: tail in a Docker container: Cannot allocate memory

question:
We're running a PHP 5.6 / Apache 2.4 container built from the official php:5.6-apache image. It is linked to a MySQL 5.6 container. HTTP on port 80 works, but HTTPS on 443 doesn't.

The Dockerfile does the following:
- installs pdo, pdo_mysql and sockets
- runs `a2enmod rewrite` and `a2enmod ssl`
- copies in a custom apache2.conf, which includes `Listen 443` inside `<IfModule ssl_module>` and `IncludeOptional sites-enabled/*.conf`
- copies 000-default.conf and default-ssl.conf into the Apache site directories
- sets `EXPOSE 443`

The Dockerfile lines are:
```
ADD 000-default.conf /etc/apache2/sites-enabled/
ADD default-ssl.conf /etc/apache2/sites-anabled/
```

default-ssl.conf defines `<VirtualHost _default_:443>` with these settings:
- `SSLEngine on`
- `SSLCertificateFile /etc/ssl/certs/site.crt`
- `SSLCertificateKeyFile /etc/ssl/certs/site.key`
- `SSLCACertificatePath /etc/ssl/certs/digicert/`

The container is started with:
```
sudo docker run -v /home/src/ssl-cert:/etc/ssl/certs --name app-gateway --link mysql56:mysql -p 80:80 -p 443:443 -d app-image
```

The image builds without errors and the container runs. HTTPS still doesn't work, and the build gives no indication of anything wrong.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The Dockerfile copies default-ssl.conf to /etc/apache2/sites-anabled/ (typo for sites-enabled). Docker silently creates that new directory, so the SSL virtual host file is never included by Apache's `IncludeOptional sites-enabled/*.conf`. Fix: Correct the ADD destination to /etc/apache2/sites-enabled/ and rebuild the image so the SSL vhost config is actually loaded.
solution: (1) Destination path in the ADD for default-ssl.conf is misspelled 'sites-anabled' (2) Docker ADD creates the nonexistent directory silently, so the build succeeds (3) Apache only includes sites-enabled/*.conf, so the 443 SSL vhost is never loaded

grounding.title: Cannot get SSL to work in Docker container

question:
We run a PostgreSQL backend for an application server. One of the operations is a trivial DELETE by primary key on a small table of about 700 rows. It normally completes in milliseconds. Intermittently, the session that ran it sits in pg_stat_activity with state 'idle in transaction' for several minutes. During those periods other work seems to stall.

To find out what is blocking, I joined pg_stat_activity to pg_locks and pg_class, ordering by query_start. I selected datname, relname, transactionid, mode, granted, usename, waiting, query, query_start, age(now(), query_start) and pid.

The output shows many RowExclusiveLock entries on the table. Every one of them has granted = true and waiting = false. I can't see any lock the session is waiting on. How do I pinpoint what causes these multi-minute delays?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The application opens a transaction, runs the DELETE, and then does not issue COMMIT or ROLLBACK for a while. The session therefore sits 'idle in transaction', and its acquired (granted) locks stay held until the transaction finally ends. This is an application bug, not a database wait. Fix: Fix the application or application server so every transaction is promptly ended with COMMIT or ROLLBACK. As a safety net only (PostgreSQL 9.6+), set idle_in_transaction_session_timeout so such sessions are rolled back and terminated automatically.
solution: (1) 'idle in transaction' means the client has not sent COMMIT/ROLLBACK; the database is not waiting on anything (2) The locks show as granted because the session already holds them; they persist until the transaction ends (3) The root cause is in the application/app server transaction handling, not PostgreSQL locking (4) idle_in_transaction_session_timeout (9.6+) is a band-aid, not the real fix

grounding.title: postgresql "idle in transaction" with all locks granted

question:
After upgrading a workstation from Ubuntu 17.10 to 18.04, installing redis-server (5:4.0.9-1) via apt fails during configuration. The postinst step reports: "Job for redis-server.service failed because a timeout was exceeded". dpkg then exits with status 1, and the dependent 'redis' metapackage is left unconfigured. systemctl shows the unit in activating (auto-restart) with Result: timeout. The ExecStart process for `/usr/bin/redis-server /etc/redis/redis.conf` exits with status 0/SUCCESS.

syslog repeatedly shows:
- `Can't open PID file /var/run/redis/redis-server.pid (yet?) after start: No such file or directory`
- `Start operation timed out. Terminating.`
- The restart counter climbing past 13.

/var/log/redis/redis-server.log shows each attempt as:
- `Redis version=4.0.9 ... Configuration loaded`
- `Creating Server TCP listening socket ::1:6379: bind: Cannot assign requested address`

The redis.conf in use is the stock file shipped with the package and has not been edited. What is preventing the service from starting?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The packaged redis.conf binds to both 127.0.0.1 and the IPv6 loopback ::1. IPv6 is disabled on this host, so binding ::1:6379 fails and Redis never comes up. systemd waits for a PID file that never appears, times out, and the dpkg postinst fails. Fix: Edit /etc/redis/redis.conf and change `bind 127.0.0.1 ::1` to `bind 127.0.0.1`. Then restart the service or rerun the package configuration, e.g. `dpkg --configure -a`.
solution: (1) Redis fails to bind ::1:6379 with 'Cannot assign requested address' (2) IPv6 is disabled or unavailable on the host (3) The default bind line includes the ::1 IPv6 loopback (4) Removing ::1 from the bind directive lets Redis start and the install complete

grounding.title: cannot install redis-server on ubuntu 18.04

question:
A small Hibernate 3.5.1 test app on Ubuntu 9.10 fails when saving an entity to PostgreSQL 8.4.3. The app is run from Eclipse with HibernateTools. Each insert fails with SQL Error: 0, SQLState: 42P01, and PostgreSQL reports that relation "public.messages" does not exist.

The mapping file maps class hello.Message to table="public.messages", with columns id (assigned generator) and messagetext.

hibernate.cfg.xml contains:
- driver org.postgresql.Driver
- user foo, password bar
- dialect PostgreSQLDialect
- show_sql=true
- hibernate.connection.url = jdbc:postgresql:postgres/tommy

When the operator connects with psql as foo and runs \d messages, the table is listed as "public.messages" with columns id integer and messagetext text. The table clearly exists from psql. Several fixes found online for this error have been tried, and none of them helped.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The JDBC URL 'jdbc:postgresql:postgres/tommy' is malformed or unusual. As a result, Hibernate connects to a different database, most likely the default 'postgres' database, instead of the one that contains the messages table. Fix: Correct the connection URL to the standard form jdbc:postgresql://hostname/databasename. Use the same host and database you pass to psql. To confirm which database the app actually connects to, enable log_connections, log_disconnections and a log_line_prefix that includes %d in postgresql.conf.
solution: (1) The JDBC URL format jdbc:postgresql:postgres/tommy is not the standard form (2) The application is connecting to the wrong database (likely the default 'postgres' DB), not the one where the table exists (3) Use jdbc:postgresql://host/dbname that matches the psql connection (4) Server connection logging with the database name (%d) can verify which DB is being hit

question:
Our Rust integration tests pass against MongoDB in our local Docker setup but fail in GitHub Actions CI.

The workflow job runs on ubuntu-latest and declares a `mongo` service container from the stock `mongo` image. It sets `MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME`, `MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD` and `MONGO_INITDB_DATABASE` from workflow env vars and maps ports `27017:27017`. No other options are set on the service. The steps are checkout, actions-rs/toolchain (stable), then actions-rs/cargo `test`.

The app builds a URI `mongodb://user:pass@<host>:27017` from `development.toml`, where host is 127.0.0.1. It creates a client and immediately runs a `ping` command. The test panics with:

```
Failed to init mongo: Error { kind: ServerSelectionError { message: "Server selection timeout: No available servers. Topology: { Type: Unknown, Servers: [ { Address: 127.0.0.1:27017, Type: Unknown, Error: Connection refused (os error 111) }, ] }" } }
```

We tried localhost, 127.0.0.1 and 0.0.0.0 as the host. All give the same connection refused.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The MongoDB service container was not yet up and accepting connections when the cargo test step ran. The service had no health check, so the job proceeded before the database was ready. Fix: Add a health check to the service via `options`, for example `--health-cmd mongo --health-interval 10s --health-timeout 5s --health-retries 5`. GitHub Actions then waits until the MongoDB container is healthy before running the steps. The working example also hardcodes the init credentials in the service env.
solution: (1) The connection refused error happens because mongod is not yet accepting connections when the tests start. (2) The host address (localhost or 127.0.0.1) is not the problem. (3) The service container had no health check, so steps began before MongoDB was ready. (4) Adding `--health-cmd` and related health options to the service makes the runner wait for readiness.

grounding.title: GitHub actions cannot connect to MongoDB service

question:
I'm building a small distributed cache in Node.js with the node_redis module and opened two Redis connections: client1 for normal commands and client2 for pub/sub. client2 subscribes to 'channel' and registers a 'message' handler that writes the received payload into 'key' via client1.set. At startup client1 sets 'key' to 'valueBefore'. After a 3-second setTimeout the script calls client2.publish('channel', 'valueAfter').

Running `node test.js` prints `Reply: OK`, then the process crashes with:
```
node_modules/redis/index.js:487
 throw new Error("Connection in pub/sub mode, only pub/sub commands may
Error: Connection in pub/sub mode, only pub/sub commands may be used
 at RedisClient.send_command (.../redis/index.js:487:15)
 at RedisClient.<anonymous> (.../redis/index.js:597:27)
 at Object._onTimeout (.../client/test.js:19:12)
```
A GET on 'key' afterwards always returns 'valueBefore'. The message handler never runs. I already use two separate clients, so I don't see why it still complains. Is running a pub/sub client and a regular client side by side not supported?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The PUBLISH is sent on client2, which entered subscriber mode when it called subscribe(). node_redis then rejects the command on that connection, the script crashes, and no message is ever delivered to the handler. Fix: Keep client2 only for subscribing and listening. Send the publish from client1, the regular connection (client1.publish('channel','valueAfter')). In general, open another connection for any non-subscriber commands.
solution: (1) client2 is in pub/sub (subscriber) mode after subscribe() (2) The publish call is made on the subscribed connection client2 (3) Publish from client1 or another non-subscribed connection (4) Regular commands need a separate connection from the subscriber connection

grounding.title: Redis / Node.js - 2 clients (1 pub/sub) causing issues with writes

question:
Our Django 1.4 app on Heroku was deployed following the official guide and worked fine at first. A day later we pushed some code changes, and since then every request fails with:

FATAL: password authentication failed for user "drjstoymyqyarj"

Running `heroku run python manage.py syncdb` dies with a traceback that ends in psycopg2.OperationalError with the same FATAL password authentication message. `heroku pg:psql` fails with the same error. `heroku run python manage.py shell` opens, but any data access inside it raises the same error.

The database settings are exactly what the Heroku docs recommend:

import dj_database_url
DATABASES = {'default': dj_database_url.config(default='postgres://localhost')}

After the push, `heroku logs` shows web.1 stopping via SIGTERM and restarting with `python ./manage.py runserver 0.0.0.0:41048 --noreload`. It reports "0 errors found" and then "Process exited with status 143" before the state goes back to up. We hadn't noticed that status line before. What's causing the authentication failures?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The app's DATABASE_URL config var no longer points to the configured Heroku Postgres database. It refers to a different or stale database/credential set, while the real database is attached under a color-named var such as HEROKU_POSTGRESQL_GREEN_URL, so connections authenticate with the wrong credentials. Fix: Run `heroku config` to check which Heroku Postgres databases are attached and what DATABASE_URL points to. Then promote the correct database to be the default with `heroku pg:promote HEROKU_POSTGRESQL_<COLOR>`, which resets DATABASE_URL to it.
solution: (1) dj_database_url reads the DATABASE_URL env var, so the credentials come from Heroku config (2) DATABASE_URL does not match the app's actual Heroku Postgres database (multiple DBs/HEROKU_POSTGRESQL_*_URL vars present) (3) Inspect with `heroku config` (4) Fix with `heroku pg:promote HEROKU_POSTGRESQL_<COLOR>`

grounding.title: "password authentication failed for user" after push to Heroku

question:
We're moving our dev environment into Docker. The image is based on node:0.12-wheezy. It creates a user `dev`, sets HOME=/home/dev, installs bower and gulp globally under ~/.npm-global, installs subversion, and drops into bash.

Our private bower registry needs a .bowerrc containing `"registry": "https://<user>:<password>@bower.mycompany.com"`, `"timeout": 300000` and `"strict-ssl": false`. We mount that file into the container with `-v /home/USER/.dockershared/.bowerrc:/home/.bowerrc`. The run also uses `--net=host` and `--privileged`, with the project mounted at /home/dev/app.

The package.json install script is `bower install -F --allow-root && node ./node_modules/svn-npm-crutch/lib/svn-npm-crutch.js`. It pulls svnDependencies from https://svn.mycompany.com.

Running `npm install` or `bower install` inside the container fails with:

```
bower ECMDERR Failed to execute "svn list https://svn.mycompany.com/repos/ui/common/tags --verbose --non-interactive", exit code of #1 svn: OPTIONS of 'https://svn.mycompany.com/repos/ui/common/tags': authorization failed: Could not authenticate to server: rejected Basic challenge (https://svn.mycompany.com)
```

The same project installs fine on the host machine. Why does it fail in the container?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: Inside the fresh container, svn has never accepted the company SVN server's SSL certificate. Bower calls svn with --non-interactive, so svn cannot prompt to accept the certificate and the svn operations fail with an authorization error. Fix: Open an interactive bash shell in the container and run `svn info` against one of the company repos, e.g. `svn info https://svn.mycompany.com/repos/ui/common/`. Accept the certificate when prompted. After that, bower/npm install works.
solution: (1) Bower runs svn with --non-interactive, so no prompts can be answered (2) The container's svn has not accepted/cached the SVN server certificate (unlike the host) (3) Running svn info interactively inside the container and accepting the certificate resolves it

grounding.title: Using private svn+bower doesn't work in dockerfile

question:
After a reboot of a CentOS host, the redis-server service will not stay up. Running `service redis-server start` returns, but the process exits almost at once. The Redis log has this as its last line before shutdown:

`Short read or OOM loading DB. Unrecoverable error, aborting now.`

Redis ran fine before the restart and its configuration was not changed. The data directory is the default /var/lib/redis, and a pid file sits at /var/run/redis.pid. The operator is new to Redis. A web search turned up no clear answer. The host otherwise seems normal after the reboot, and Redis will not start no matter how many times it is retried.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The persisted snapshot /var/lib/redis/dump.rdb is truncated or corrupted. When Redis tries to load it at startup it hits a short read and aborts. Fix: Stop Redis and remove the bad /var/lib/redis/dump.rdb, plus the stale /var/run/redis.pid. Then start the service again with `service redis-server start`. Removing the file permanently deletes the stored data, so restore from a backup first if the data matters.
solution: (1) The failure happens while Redis loads its RDB file (dump.rdb) at startup (2) The dump.rdb file is truncated or corrupted, which causes the 'Short read' abort (3) Removing or replacing dump.rdb, and clearing the stale pid file, lets Redis start (4) Deleting dump.rdb loses the persisted data, so take or restore a backup first

grounding.title: Short read or OOM loading DB. Unrecoverable error, aborting now

question:
Our reporting tool stores generated reports in the PHP session as $_SESSION['report_name_<unixtimestamp>'] = gzcompress(serialize($report)) so users can later export the exact report they viewed (PDF, Excel). The export endpoint reads the key from a GET parameter, then decompresses and unserializes it. This worked fine with file-based sessions. After moving sessions to Redis through a custom save handler registered before session_start(), the behavior changed. We tried both the phpredis extension and Predis. The first report run in a session exports correctly. When the same user runs the report again, a new timestamped key should appear next to the old one, but the export fails with "file doesn't exist". In Redis the session blob still holds the older report key and the newer one is missing. Dumping $_SESSION during the report request shows the new key is present, yet it never persists. Redis has plenty of memory. The report class is included before unserialize. Stepping through with xdebug and breakpoints makes the export work. Without breakpoints it fails. Adding sleep() calls in places didn't help. The report page also issues several AJAX calls to the server.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The custom Redis session save handler has no session locking. Concurrent AJAX requests from the report page read the session before the new report is saved. When they finish, they write back their stale copy and overwrite the session that contains the new report. Fix: Prevent concurrent requests from clobbering the session. One way is to implement locking in the Redis save handler, as file sessions do. Another is to have the parallel AJAX requests avoid writing the session, for example by calling session_write_close early or using read-only sessions.
solution: (1) The custom Redis save handler lacks the session locking that file sessions provide. (2) Parallel AJAX requests on the report page read the session before the report is stored. (3) Those requests write their older session copy at shutdown, overwriting the new report key (last write wins). (4) It is a timing race, which explains why debugging with breakpoints makes it work.
technology: PHP sessions with Redis (phpredis/Predis custom save handler)

grounding.title: PHP Redis Session not saving

answer: Root cause: Nginx resolves the proxy_pass hostname when it loads its configuration and no resolver is configured for that location. When the backend name can no longer be resolved, nginx hits a fatal [emerg] and the whole process refuses to start. Fix: Add a resolver directive (for example `resolver 8.8.8.8;`) inside the location or server block that proxies to the backend, so a down or unresolvable upstream does not crash nginx. Prefer a trusted internal DNS server over a public one, because public DNS responses can be spoofed.
solution: (1) The error comes from nginx failing to resolve the upstream hostname in proxy_pass when it loads the config (2) One unresolvable upstream is fatal ([emerg]) and stops the whole nginx process, not just that vhost (3) Adding a resolver directive in the proxy location prevents the crash (4) Using a public resolver carries a DNS spoofing risk; a secure or internal DNS server is preferable

grounding.title: Docker Nginx stopped: [emerg] 1#1: host not found in upstream

question:
We stood up Redis on an EC2 instance and can't reach it from another machine. From my workstation:

$ redis-cli -h ec2-75-101-204-XXX.compute-1.amazonaws.com
Could not connect to Redis at ec2-75-101-204-XXX.compute-1.amazonaws.com:6379: Operation timed out

The instance's Security Group has an inbound rule allowing TCP 6379. On the Redis host, netstat (run as non-root) shows:

tcp 0 0 127.0.0.1:6379 0.0.0.0:* LISTEN
tcp 0 0 0.0.0.0:22 0.0.0.0:* LISTEN
tcp6 0 0 :::22 :::* LISTEN

SSH to the box works fine. The redis.conf in use contains:

daemonize yes
pidfile /var/run/redis.pid
port 6379
timeout 300
loglevel notice
logfile /var/log/redis.log
databases 16
save 900 1 / save 300 10 / save 60 10000
stop-writes-on-bgsave-error yes
rdbcompression yes

The server is up and the port is open in the Security Group. Why are remote connections timing out?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: Redis is listening only on the loopback interface (127.0.0.1:6379), so it doesn't accept connections arriving on the instance's external interface. The Security Group is not the cause. Fix: Edit the redis.conf actually in use (often /etc/redis/redis.conf). Replace `bind 127.0.0.1` with `bind 0.0.0.0`, or add that line if there is no bind directive. Then restart Redis.
solution: (1) netstat shows Redis listening on 127.0.0.1:6379 rather than 0.0.0.0 (2) Redis is bound to localhost only, so remote clients cannot connect (3) Change the bind directive in redis.conf to 0.0.0.0 (or the external interface) and restart

grounding.title: Connection to redis is timing out

question:
We containerize a Python app that relies heavily on numpy. The Dockerfile is based on `python:3.6`. It sets the timezone, copies requirements.txt, and runs `pip install -r requirements.txt`. requirements.txt pins numpy==1.14.3 alongside other deps.

The image builds fine on a developer's macOS laptop. On our Raspberry Pi hosts (Raspbian stretch/buster), the build never gets past numpy. Output:

```
Step 6/15 : RUN pip install numpy==1.14.3
Collecting numpy==1.14.3
 Downloading https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/.../numpy-1.14.3.zip (4.9MB)
Building wheels for collected packages: numpy
 Building wheel for numpy (setup.py): started
 Building wheel for numpy (setup.py): still running...
 Building wheel for numpy (setup.py): still running...
```

It then fails. Moving numpy out of requirements.txt into its own RUN step made no difference. Other packages install fine. We need numpy to install reliably in the Pi build.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: On the Raspberry Pi (ARM) host, pip downloads the numpy source zip rather than a prebuilt wheel, so numpy has to be compiled inside the container. The image lacks the native build dependencies numpy needs, such as a C compiler, a Fortran compiler, Python dev headers and libc dev headers, so the wheel build fails. Fix: Install numpy's build dependencies in the image before running pip: python3-dev, gcc, gfortran and musl-dev (e.g. `apk add --no-cache python3 python3-dev gcc gfortran musl-dev` on an Alpine base). Then upgrade pip/setuptools and run `pip install -r requirements.txt`.
solution: (1) pip is building numpy from the source zip (setup.py wheel build), not installing a prebuilt binary (2) The ARM host differs from macOS, where the build succeeds (3) numpy compilation requires native toolchain packages: gcc, gfortran, python3-dev, musl-dev (4) Fix by installing those build deps and upgrading pip before installing requirements
technology: Docker / Python numpy on Raspberry Pi (ARM)

grounding.title: Install Numpy Requirement in a Dockerfile. Results in error

question:
On a Mac I'm containerizing a basic ASP.NET demo built from the yo aspnet 'Empty Application' template. Running it directly with `dnx web` works: Kestrel prints 'Hosting environment: Production / Now listening on: http://localhost:5000 / Application started' and the browser shows 'Hello World!' at http://localhost:5000.

Inside Docker it doesn't work. The image builds fine. The Dockerfile has `EXPOSE 5000` and I start the container with `docker run -i -t -p 5000:5000 container_name`. Kestrel prints the same startup lines, including 'Now listening on: http://localhost:5000'. But http://localhost:5000 in the browser gives ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED.

Docker reports it is using the default machine at 192.168.99.100. http://192.168.99.100:5000 also returns ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED. `docker inspect container_name | grep IPAddress` shows the container IP is 172.17.0.2. Browsing http://172.17.0.2:5000 just spins and then times out. How do I reach the app from my browser?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: Kestrel inside the container listens only on localhost (http://localhost:5000). Traffic forwarded by Docker's port mapping does not arrive on the container's loopback interface, so nothing answers it. The container IP 172.17.0.2 is not reachable from the Mac. The correct address is the Docker VM at 192.168.99.100. Fix: Make Kestrel bind to all interfaces by changing the Dockerfile entrypoint to `ENTRYPOINT ["dnx", "web", "--server.urls", "http://0.0.0.0:5000"]`. Then run with a port mapping such as `-p 80:5000` and browse to the VM IP, http://192.168.99.100.
solution: (1) Kestrel is bound to localhost inside the container, so it is unreachable through Docker's forwarded port (2) The server must listen on 0.0.0.0 (for example via --server.urls http://0.0.0.0:5000) (3) On Mac with docker-machine, browse to the VM IP 192.168.99.100, not localhost and not the container IP 172.17.0.2 (4) The -p port mapping is what links host and container ports; EXPOSE alone is not sufficient

grounding.title: ASP.NET on Docker Not Serving Web App to Browser

question:
On an Ubuntu 12.04 host (EC2 base AMI), redis-server was installed with apt-get. It refuses to start. The startup output shows:

*** FATAL CONFIG FILE ERROR ***
Reading the configuration file, at line 56
>>> 'tcp-keepalive 0'
Bad directive or wrong number of arguments

The config file in use is the full commented example redis.conf. It has daemonize no, pidfile /var/run/redis.pid, port 6379, timeout 0, a long commented 'TCP keepalive' section ending in 'tcp-keepalive 0', then loglevel notice, logfile stdout, databases 16, and the snapshotting section. The line looks syntactically correct: one directive and one numeric argument, matching the comments above it. Nobody has hand-edited the file in a way that would explain a typo. The server does not get past config parsing.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The config file is the example redis.conf for Redis 2.6, but the installed server is the old 2.2.x package from Ubuntu's repository. That version does not recognize the tcp-keepalive directive, so it rejects it as a bad directive. Fix: Comment out or delete the tcp-keepalive line. Another option is to use the example config file that matches the installed Redis version. Or upgrade Redis to a newer version, for example from the rwky/redis PPA, which installs 2.8.x.
solution: (1) Installed Redis version (2.2.x from Ubuntu apt) is older than the config file's version (2.6 example) (2) tcp-keepalive directive is not supported in older Redis (2.2/2.4) (3) Check the version with dpkg -s redis-server and match the config to it, or remove the line / upgrade Redis

grounding.title: Redis server not starting

question:
I'm setting up remote debugging of a Go program from my editor (Atom) into a Docker container. Docker runs on a Mac host, and the debugger is Delve inside the container. In a shell in the container, I installed Delve with `go get github.com/derekparker/delve/cmd/dlv`. Running `dlv debug hello.go` in /go/src/app fails immediately with:

```
could not launch process: fork/exec ./debug: operation not permitted
```

I'm already root in the container. Trying `sudo` just gives `bash: sudo: command not found`. Because Delve on macOS normally needs code signing, I codesigned on the Mac host as well. That changed nothing, and I wouldn't expect host signing to matter inside a Linux container anyway. The program builds fine, so only launching it under the debugger fails. What is blocking Delve, and how do I get it working inside the container?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The container runs with Docker's default restricted privileges. These block the operations Delve needs to launch and trace the debug binary, so fork/exec fails with 'operation not permitted' even for root inside the container. Host-side macOS code signing is unrelated. Fix: Start the container with `docker run --privileged ...` so Delve has the privileges it needs to launch and debug the process.
solution: (1) The error comes from Docker's default container security restrictions, not missing root or sudo inside the container (2) Codesigning on the macOS host doesn't affect a Linux container (3) Running the container with --privileged resolves the error

grounding.title: fork/exec ./debug: operation not permitted

question:
A CentOS 7 VPS accepts interactive SSH logins for 'user' without trouble, but SFTP sessions to the same host fail. The client is a Mac running OpenSSH_6.9p1/LibreSSL 2.1.8, and the server reports OpenSSH_6.6.1. Running `sftp -v user@example.org` shows the connection being established and authentication succeeding. After that the session closes, and the client reports exit status 127.

The sshd_config came from a template. Relevant lines:
```
Port 22
Protocol 2
UsePrivilegeSeparation yes
PermitRootLogin no
PubkeyAuthentication yes
PasswordAuthentication yes
X11Forwarding no
AcceptEnv LANG LC_*
#Subsystem sftp /usr/lib/openssh/sftp-server
Subsystem sftp /usr/lib/openssh/sftp-server
UsePAM yes
AllowUsers user@xx.xxx.xx.xxx user@xx.xxx.xx.xxx apt-dater@xx.xxx.xx.xxx
Match User user
 PasswordAuthentication yes
```

The user is allowed by AllowUsers, and the same credentials work for a normal shell. Only the file transfer subsystem fails.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The Subsystem sftp directive points to /usr/lib/openssh/sftp-server, a Debian-style path that does not exist on this CentOS server. When sshd tries to execute it, the command is not found, giving exit status 127. Fix: Change the Subsystem directive to the server's actual sftp-server path (on CentOS, typically /usr/libexec/openssh/sftp-server), or use `Subsystem sftp internal-sftp`. Then restart sshd.
solution: (1) Exit status 127 means the command executed for the sftp subsystem was not found (2) The Subsystem sftp path /usr/lib/openssh/sftp-server does not exist on the server (3) Fix by pointing Subsystem at an existing sftp-server binary or using internal-sftp, then restart sshd

grounding.title: Can connect via SSH - but not via SFTP? Exit status 127

question:
We run MySQL server inside a VirtualBox guest (NAT networking). We need to reach it from a client on the host machine. NAT port forwarding for the MySQL port is configured and verified. Every connection attempt from the host, whatever the client tool, fails with the same message:

```
Host '10.0.2.2' is not allowed to connect to this MySQL server
```

We are trying to log in as root. In my.cnf we confirmed these lines are present:
```
skip-external-locking
bind-address = 0.0.0.0
```
The error did not change. We also tried `bind-address = 10.0.2.2`, but then the MySQL service failed to start at all, so we reverted it. Connections from inside the VM work. What is preventing the host from connecting?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The server is reachable over the network. The root account is only defined for localhost, which is the default on most installs. The mysql.user table has no row whose Host value (such as '%' or '10.0.2.2') matches the client address 10.0.2.2, so the server rejects the connection. Fix: Run `select user,host from mysql.user where user='root';` to check the current entries. Then create a root account for the client host and grant it privileges: `create user 'root'@'10.0.2.2' identified by 'pw'; grant all privileges on *.* to 'root'@'10.0.2.2' with grant option; flush privileges;`.
solution: (1) The error is an authentication/authorization rejection, not a network or bind-address problem (2) Root is localhost-only by default; mysql.user has no Host entry matching 10.0.2.2 or % (3) Create or grant a user for 'root'@'10.0.2.2' (or '%') and flush privileges (4) bind-address must be a local interface address; 10.0.2.2 is the NAT gateway/host side, so the server could not start with it

grounding.title: Access to MySQL server via VirtualBox

question:
On a dual-homed Linux test server, adding a static route out of the internal interface fails. Interfaces: eth0 is 192.168.36.132 with mask 255.255.254.0, and eth1 is a public 116.x.x.x/26 address that carries the default route.

Command run:
`route add -net 10.248.12.0 netmask 255.255.255.240 gw 192.168.36.254 dev eth0`

It returns: `SIOCADDRT: Network is unreachable`

`ip route list` shows:
```
116.66.240.64/26 dev eth1 proto kernel scope link src 116.xx.xx.xx
192.168.238.0/24 via 192.168.36.254 dev eth0
192.168.239.0/24 via 192.168.36.254 dev eth0
192.168.36.0/23 via 192.168.36.254 dev eth0
169.254.0.0/16 dev eth0 scope link
127.0.0.0/8 dev lo scope link
default via 116.xx.xx.xx dev eth1
```
`netstat -anr` agrees. It lists 192.168.36.0/255.255.254.0 with gateway 192.168.36.254 and flags UG on eth0.

The operator has spent several days on this and cannot work out why the kernel rejects the 192.168.36.254 gateway. That address sits inside eth0's own address range.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The 192.168.36.0/23 network that eth0 sits on is routed via gateway 192.168.36.254 instead of being a directly connected (scope link) route. As a result the kernel has no on-link route to reach 192.168.36.254 itself. Any route that uses it as a next hop is therefore rejected as unreachable. Fix: Delete the gateway-based route for 192.168.36.0/23. Replace it with a directly connected route, for example `ip route add 192.168.36.0/23 dev eth0` (shown as scope link, flags U, gateway 0.0.0.0). Then re-add the static route via 192.168.36.254.
solution: (1) The 192.168.36.0/23 route is wrongly marked UG via 192.168.36.254 instead of being a link-local (scope link) route (2) With no on-link route for that subnet, the kernel cannot reach the gateway 192.168.36.254 as a neighbour, so it reports SIOCADDRT Network is unreachable (3) The fix is to replace the gateway route with `ip route add 192.168.36.0/23 dev eth0` (no gateway)

grounding.title: Unable to add a static route: SIOADDRT: Network is unreachable

question:
A small Arch Linux server keeps most of its data on an md RAID-1 (md16) built from two SATA disks. After about 4 months of normal service, the kernel log began showing repeated read failures on one member, sdd. Typical entries:

```
ata5.01: failed command: READ DMA EXT
... Emask 0x9 (media error)
ata5.01: error: { UNC }
sd 4:0:1:0: [sdd] Sense Key : Medium Error [current]
sd 4:0:1:0: [sdd] Add. Sense: Unrecovered read error - auto reallocate failed
end_request: I/O error, dev sdd, sector 657746444
md/raid1:md16: read error corrected (8 sectors at 657744392 on sdd1)
md/raid1:md16: redirecting sector 657742336 to other mirror: sdd1
```

Each error named a different sector and caused a multi-second stall. They appeared mostly during backups, but also on roughly every fifth save of a small text file.

smartctl on sdd reports:
- Raw_Read_Error_Rate raw 1606
- Reallocated_Sector_Ct 0
- Reallocated_Event_Count 0
- Current_Pending_Sector 51

A replacement disk was ordered. A day later the errors stopped completely. There was no reboot and nothing was changed. Later the disk was removed from the array and re-added, and it still behaves normally. Why did the errors stop?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: A physical region of the platter went bad. The drive flagged those sectors as pending, but it could not remap them while they still held data, so every read of them failed. Once the sectors were overwritten (md rewriting the data from the good mirror, or the resync), the drive remapped them to spare sectors and the read errors stopped. Fix: Overwrite the bad sectors so the drive can remap them, for example via md's correction from the mirror, a RAID resync, or zeroing/reformatting the disk. After that, monitor SMART reallocated and pending counts, and replace the disk if more of the surface starts to fail.
solution: (1) Unreadable sectors are marked pending (Current_Pending_Sector) but cannot be remapped while they hold data that can't be read (2) Writing to or overwriting those sectors lets the drive remap them to spares (3) md RAID-1 rewrites failed sectors from the other mirror, and a re-add/resync overwrites the disk, which triggered the remapping (4) After remapping, the errors stop unless more media fails, so the drive should still be monitored
technology: Linux md RAID / SATA HDD SMART

grounding.title: Hard drive read errors that... stop?

question:
Our home gateway runs Snort in inline mode through NFQUEUE. Four Snort processes read queues 0-3 via an iptables rule: `NFQUEUE balance 0:3 bypass cpu-fanout`. New inbound TCP/80 connections from one allowed remote host jump to a chain that NFLOGs and then queues them. Established traffic is sent to Snort through a separate chain.

Rules come from Emerging Threats via pulledpork. One example is sid:2017590, the D-Link backdoor User-Agent rule:

`alert tcp $EXTERNAL_NET any -> $HOME_NET $HTTP_PORTS (... content:"xmlset_roodkcableoj28840ybtide"; http_header; ...)`

To test it, lighttpd was started on the gateway itself, listening on port 80 of its WAN interface. From a remote host I ran:

`curl -A 'xmlset_roodkcableoj28840ybtide' 'http://<EXTERNAL_IP>'`

The page comes back immediately and Snort logs no alert. The iptables counters show packets hitting the NFQUEUE rule, so Snort is receiving traffic.

During BitTorrent load, only the Snort processes on CPUs 1 and 2 get busy, while those on CPUs 0 and 3 stay idle. I have already reviewed the iptables/NFQUEUE setup, the systemd units and the alert output, and found nothing obviously wrong.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The test traffic was aimed at the gateway's own public IP, which is not part of $HOME_NET (only the LAN subnets are). Rules written as $EXTERNAL_NET any -> $HOME_NET therefore never match that traffic, so Snort processes the packets but raises no alert. Fix: Test against a host or address inside the defined HOME_NET, such as a LAN server reached through the gateway. Alternatively, include the gateway's public IP in HOME_NET if traffic to the gateway itself should be inspected.
solution: (1) Snort is receiving packets; the issue is rule matching, not packet delivery (2) The rule's direction is $EXTERNAL_NET -> $HOME_NET (3) The gateway's own public/WAN IP is not part of HOME_NET (only LAN subnets are) (4) Traffic to the gateway's public IP does not match the rule, so the testing method is at fault
technology: Snort inline IPS with iptables NFQUEUE

grounding.title: Snort is receiving traffic, but doesn't appear to be applying rules

question:
We run nginx 1.8.0 on Debian (OpenSSL 1.0.1f) as a TLS-terminating reverse proxy for several sites on the same box. One of those sites has to pass PCI DSS, and the latest Trustwave scan failed it because TLS 1.0 is still accepted. The http block in nginx.conf has `ssl_protocols TLSv1 TLSv1.1 TLSv1.2;`. The server block for the PCI site sets `ssl_protocols TLSv1.1 TLSv1.2;`. We have also tried moving the SSL directives out of the http block into each SSL server block and changing the cipher list. After every change and reload, `openssl s_client -connect www.example.com:443 -tls1` still completes a TLS 1.0 handshake. SSL Labs rates the site A but lists TLS 1.0 as enabled. The other SSL settings appear correct. Only the protocol restriction for this one site seems to have no effect.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The site shares an IP:port with other virtual hosts, and nginx selects the server block from SNI. The TLS protocol version is negotiated before SNI chooses that server block, so the per-server ssl_protocols cannot take effect. The protocols of the default/first server on that listener are used instead. Fix: Give the PCI site its own dedicated IP address with no other virtual hosts on it. nginx can then apply that server's ssl_protocols (TLSv1.1 TLSv1.2) based on the IP and refuse TLS 1.0.
solution: (1) Multiple SNI-based virtual hosts share the same IP:443 (2) Protocol version is negotiated before the SNI-selected server block applies (3) The per-server ssl_protocols is effectively ignored (4) Fix by binding the site to a dedicated IP so its settings apply at connection time

grounding.title: Disable TLS 1.0 in NGINX

question:
While chasing slow performance on our office network, I ran traceroute against several large public sites. Most destinations complete. yahoo.com, amazon.com and ebay.com never do, and the result repeats every time.

Example against ebay.com, run with the default traceroute and no options:
```
traceroute: Warning: ebay.com has multiple addresses; using 66.135.205.13
traceroute to ebay.com (66.135.205.13), 64 hops max, 52 byte packets
 1 10.10.100.1  56.518 ms 2.390 ms 2.082 ms
 2 mo-69-34-118-1.sta.embarqhsd.net  9.943 ms ...
 ...
 8 ae-2-52.edge4.chicago3.level3.net  27.137 ms ...
 9 chp-brdr-03.inet.qwest.net  26.315 ms ...
10 dvr-edge-13.inet.qwest.net  51.270 ms 51.355 ms 51.134 ms
11 * * *
12 * * *
...
33 * * *
34 * *^C
```
Latency looks normal through hop 10. After that every probe times out until I cancel. Is something on our side breaking these traces, and does it relate to our performance problem?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The destination networks use firewalls that filter the traffic default traceroute relies on: UDP probes to unlikely high ports, and/or the ICMP replies. Hops past their edge therefore never answer. This reflects filtering on the target networks, not a fault in the operator's network. Fix: Use a traceroute method that firewalls are likely to allow. `traceroute -I` sends ICMP echo probes and `traceroute -T` sends TCP SYN probes; either should get further or complete (yahoo.com completes this way).
solution: (1) Default traceroute probes (UDP to high ports, relying on ICMP responses) are filtered by firewalls on the destination networks (2) The asterisks after the provider edge reflect that filtering, not packet loss or a performance problem in the local network (3) Using ICMP echo (-I) or TCP SYN (-T) probe methods works around the filtering

grounding.title: Why does traceroute fail for amazon.com, yahoo.com, and ebay.com?

question:
Users get HTTP 502 Bad Gateway when requesting a PHP page under a subdirectory (http://domain.com/dev/index.php). Static content on the same nginx server appears to work. This is the first time the operator has seen this error on the box.

The nginx error log has this entry for each failed request:

2011/09/30 23:47:54 [error] 31160#0: *35 connect() failed (111: Connection refused) while connecting to upstream, client: xx.xx.xx.xx, server: domain.com, request: "GET /dev/ HTTP/1.1", upstream: "fastcgi://127.0.0.1:9000", host: "domain.com"

nginx.conf is a stock Debian/Ubuntu-style config: user www-data, 4 worker processes, 768 worker_connections, sendfile and gzip on, logging to /var/log/nginx/, and includes for conf.d/*.conf and sites-enabled/*. A site config sends .php requests to FastCGI at 127.0.0.1:9000. Nothing has been changed yet.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: No FastCGI/PHP backend (php-fpm) is running and listening on 127.0.0.1:9000. nginx tries to hand the PHP request to that upstream, the TCP connection is refused, and nginx returns 502. Fix: Install and start php-fpm and configure it to listen on 127.0.0.1:9000. Make sure nginx has a `location ~ \.php$` block with `fastcgi_pass 127.0.0.1:9000;`, then reload nginx.
solution: (1) Error 111 Connection refused means nothing is listening on the upstream address 127.0.0.1:9000 (2) The upstream is a FastCGI PHP backend (php-fpm) that is not running or not configured (3) nginx itself is fine; the 502 comes from the missing backend (4) Starting php-fpm on port 9000 and pointing fastcgi_pass at it resolves the error

grounding.title: connect() failed (111: Connection refused) while connecting to upstream

question:
Synology DS212+ (ARM, DSM 4.1) NAS. I installed bash and set it as the login shell for several accounts. root, with /bin/bash in /etc/passwd, logs in over SSH with no trouble. A regular account (joeuser, uid 1029, shell /bin/bash) authenticates fine. The 'Last login' banner prints, then the session immediately shows 'Permission denied, please try again.' and the connection closes. If I switch joeuser's shell back to /bin/sh, SSH login works. With /bin/bash the same user can log in on the serial console, and 'su - joeuser' as root also works, so the bash binary itself is fine. As a test I changed joeuser's uid to 0, and SSH still failed. sshd_config has UsePAM yes, PermitRootLogin yes, ChrootDirectory none, and an internal-sftp subsystem, with nothing unusual. I ran the vendor daemon in debug mode (/usr/syno/sbin/sshd -d, OpenSSH_5.8p1-hpn13v11) with LogLevel DEBUG. Nothing in the output explains the rejection.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: Synology's sshd is a vendor-modified OpenSSH build. In do_child() (session.c) it calls a hard-coded IsAllowShell() check. That check grants shell sessions only to the usernames root or admin, or to users whose passwd shell is exactly /bin/sh or /bin/ash. Any other user/shell combination gets 'Permission denied, please try again.' and the process exits, whatever the uid. Fix: Rebuild Synology's OpenSSH 5.8p1 source (from their GPL release) with the IsAllowShell() check removed. Cross-compile it for the NAS CPU (Marvell Kirkwood) and replace the vendor sshd binary. Alternatively, keep users on /bin/sh or /bin/ash.
solution: (1) Synology ships a customized OpenSSH sshd, not stock OpenSSH (2) A hard-coded check (IsAllowShell) in session.c allows only /bin/sh or /bin/ash for users other than root/admin (3) The check goes by username and shell string, not uid, which is why uid=0 didn't help (4) Fix is to recompile sshd without that check (or use an allowed shell)

grounding.title: Can't log in via SSH to any accounts using /bin/bash shell on Synology NAS

question:
Our small company domain is hosted on Google Apps, and every user sends through the Gmail web interface. For the past few weeks our inbox has been filling with delivery-failure notices. Each one concerns mail that appears to come from a random, nonexistent mailbox on our domain, e.g. onSecNtV1@ourdomain.com, sent to strangers. The admin console shows no unusual account activity and no unknown users. I looked for a setting to block sending from unregistered addresses and found none.

Sample bounce: "Google tried to deliver your message, but it was rejected by the server for the recipient domain 174.133.125.2 ... 553 sorry, that domain isn't in my list of allowed rcpthosts (#5.7.1)". The quoted original contains:
- an X-Google-DKIM-Signature with d=google.com, s=20120113
- Return-Path <onSecNtV1@ourdomain.com>
- Received: from [117.201.44.87] ([117.201.34.157]) by mx.google.com
- Received-SPF: neutral (117.201.34.157 is neither permitted nor denied by best guess record for domain ...)
- Subject "I will be excited if you are my Valetine"

The DKIM header and the "Google tried to deliver" wording make me worry the spam originates from our own trusted clients. Where is the leak?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The Google Apps domain has a catch-all address enabled. All mail addressed to any random, nonexistent username at the domain, including spam and bounce backscatter for spoofed senders, is accepted and delivered to the admin's mailbox. The X-Google-DKIM-Signature header is a Gmail-internal header, not a DKIM signature for the customer's domain, so it does not show the mail came from the user's accounts. Fix: Disable the catch-all address setting in the Google Apps admin console so mail for nonexistent users is rejected. Ignore the X-Google-DKIM-Signature header. If real domain authentication is wanted, set up DKIM signing for the domain in Google Apps.
solution: (1) A catch-all address is enabled, so mail to any random username at the domain is delivered to a real mailbox (2) The bounces for random usernames are spoofed or backscatter traffic, not proof that an account was compromised (3) X-Google-DKIM-Signature (d=google.com) is Gmail-specific and is not a DKIM signature for the user's domain (4) The domain has no real DKIM for its own name and no SPF record (SPF result is 'neutral', based on a best guess); real domain DKIM must be configured separately
technology: Google Apps (G Suite) email / DKIM / SPF

grounding.title: How did spammer spoof emails with my google apps domain (it even has DKIM!)

question:
I'm automating setup of an AWS EC2 Ubuntu instance as part of a build pipeline and need to enable IPv4 forwarding non-interactively. Manual edits aren't an option. The build step runs this:

```
sudo echo "net.ipv4.ip_forward = 1" >> /etc/sysctl.conf
```

It fails with:

```
Permission denied
```

This is confusing because sudo has worked for every other privileged command in the same script, such as package installs and service restarts. In an interactive SSH session, if I run `sudo su` first and then the same echo/append line, it works and the line ends up in /etc/sysctl.conf. I need a way to make this work from the script without dropping into an interactive root shell or editing the file by hand.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The `>>` redirection is performed by the calling, unprivileged shell before sudo runs. Only `echo` gets elevated, so the shell opening /etc/sysctl.conf for append is denied. Fix: Run the whole command, including the redirection, under root. For example: `sudo /bin/su -c "echo 'net.ipv4.ip_forward = 1' >> /etc/sysctl.conf"`. Alternatively, copy the file to /tmp, append there, and `sudo cp` it back to /etc.
solution: (1) Redirection (>, >>, <) is handled by the calling shell, not the command run via sudo (2) sudo only elevates the echo process, not the file open for append (3) The fix is to run the redirection inside a root shell (sudo su -c / sh -c) or write elsewhere and sudo cp the file back

grounding.title: `sudo echo "bla" >> /etc/sysctl.conf` permission denied

question:
Setting up a first test OpenLDAP server on Ubuntu, following the distro's basic setup guide. I wrote an LDIF that creates ou=People and ou=Groups (organizationalUnit), a group cn=engineers with objectClass posixGroup and gidNumber 5000, and a user uid=john with objectClasses inetOrgPerson, posixAccount and shadowAccount (uidNumber 10000, gidNumber 5000, loginShell, homeDirectory, gecos, userPassword).

Loaded it with:
  ldapadd -x -D cn=admin,dc=example,dc=com -W -f add_content.ldif

The two OUs seem fine, but the group and user entries fail:
  adding new entry "cn=engineers,ou=Groups,dc=my-domain,dc=com"
  ldap_add: Invalid syntax (21)
    additional info: objectClass: value #0 invalid per syntax
  adding new entry "uid=john,ou=People,dc=my-domain,dc=com"
  ldap_add: Invalid syntax (21)
    additional info: objectClass: value #0 invalid per syntax

Server is configured through a slapd.conf file. Searching the error message turned up nothing useful. Why are these entries rejected?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The nis schema, which defines the posixGroup, posixAccount and shadowAccount object classes, isn't loaded in slapd. The server treats those objectClass values as unknown and rejects them as invalid syntax. Fix: With slapd.conf, add an include line for nis.schema (e.g. include /usr/local/etc/openldap/schema/nis.schema, adjusting the path) and restart slapd. With cn=config, load nis.ldif instead, e.g. ldapadd -Y EXTERNAL -H ldapi:// -f .../nis.ldif. No restart is needed in that case.
solution: (1) posixGroup/posixAccount/shadowAccount come from the nis schema (2) nis schema is not loaded in the server (3) Fix by including nis.schema in slapd.conf and restarting slapd (or ldapadd nis.ldif under cn=config)

grounding.title: Why does this ldapadd command quit with an "Invalid syntax" error?

question:
We need to fetch https://www.lawsociety.com.au with curl from two machines. On an Ubuntu 16.04 box (curl 7.47.0) it works: the verbose output shows the session negotiated as TLS1.0 / RSA_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA1, the certificate verifies, and we get HTTP/1.1 200 OK from Oracle-Application-Server-11g. On Windows 10 with curl 7.57.0 (x86_64-pc-win32) libcurl/7.57.0 OpenSSL/1.1.0g (WinSSL), the same request fails immediately after the client sends its hello:

* TLSv1.2 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS alert, Server hello (2):
curl: (35) error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure

The CA bundle loads without problems (D:\dev\curl\bin\curl-ca-bundle.crt). We also tried openssl s_client from Windows and passing --ciphers RC4-SHA to curl, and neither connected. Why does the Windows client fail when the Linux one succeeds?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The server is badly outdated. It supports only SSLv3/TLS1.0 and four cipher suites: DES-CBC-SHA, DES-CBC3-SHA, RC4-MD5 and RC4-SHA. OpenSSL 1.1.0g, used by the Windows curl, has dropped single-DES entirely and disables RC4 and 3DES by default, so the two sides share no cipher and the server sends a handshake_failure alert. The older Ubuntu stack still allows 3DES. Fix: Explicitly re-enable a legacy cipher the server supports, such as 3DES (DES-CBC3-SHA) or RC4, in the OpenSSL-based client. This only works if the cipher was not compiled out of the build, and the WinSSL/schannel backend may ignore OpenSSL cipher names. The proper fix is for the server operator to upgrade to modern TLS versions and ciphers.
solution: (1) The server supports only SSLv3/TLS1.0 with DES, 3DES and RC4 cipher suites. (2) OpenSSL 1.1.0g removes single-DES and disables RC4 and 3DES by default. (3) With no cipher in common, the server aborts with a handshake_failure alert. (4) Ubuntu 16.04's older TLS library still negotiates 3DES, which is why it works there.

grounding.title: curl fails to retrieve HTTPS content: error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure

question:
Local Ubuntu 12.04 box running nginx 1.1.19. nginx.conf is stock apart from the user directive, now `user nginx www-data;`. A test vhost serves static files with `root /home;`, `index index.html`, `server_name localhost`, and `try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html`.

A page at /home/index.html loads fine at http://localhost/. I changed root to /home/ubuntu, moved the file to /home/ubuntu/index.html, recreated the sites-enabled symlink, and stopped and started nginx. Now every request returns 403 Forbidden.

The file itself shows `-rw-r--r-- 1 nginx www-data 183 ... index.html`. Running chmod 777 on it made no difference. `/etc/init.d/nginx configtest` reports no errors, and the symlink is correct.

The same behaviour appears on an EC2 Ubuntu 12.04 instance. I wondered whether home-directory encryption is involved, but I can't see why content under the user's home folder can't be served when the same file one level up works.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The user's home directory /home/ubuntu has default permissions 700 on Ubuntu 12.04, so the nginx worker user has no execute (traverse) permission on that parent directory. It therefore cannot reach the file, whatever the file's own permissions are. Fix: Give others execute permission on the home directory with `chmod 701 /home/ubuntu` (or 755). Make sure every directory on the path to the web root is executable by the nginx user/group, and every served file is readable by it.
solution: (1) Ubuntu home directories default to mode 700 (2) nginx needs execute permission on every parent directory along the path, not just read on the file (3) Changing the file's own permissions (even 777) does not help when a parent directory blocks traversal (4) Fix: chmod 701 or 755 on the home directory

grounding.title: nginx 403 Forbidden Error hosting in User Home Directory

question:
Our CentOS 6 OpenVZ host lost NAT on the host itself, and we are not aware of any intentional change. Running as root:

$ iptables -t nat -L
iptables v1.4.7: can't initialize iptables table `nat': Table does not exist (do you need to insmod?)
Perhaps iptables or your kernel needs to be upgraded.

The running kernel is 2.6.32-042stab088.4. Booting the older OpenVZ kernels 042stab085.20 and 042stab084.26 gives the same error. No further updates are available.

Recent package history: vzctl-4.7.2-1 and vzctl-core-4.7.2-1 were installed on May 5. Before that, util-linux-ng and libblkid on Apr 30, and vzkernel 088.4, nss-softokn, bridge-utils and openssl in April.

lsmod shows iptable_nat, nf_nat, nf_conntrack_ipv4, nf_conntrack, ip_tables, iptable_filter and iptable_mangle all loaded. vzrst and vzcpt depend on nf_conntrack.

`modprobe /lib/modules/.../iptable_nat.ko` fails with "Module not found", even though the .ko file exists at that path.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The vzctl upgrade from 4.6 to 4.7 changed the default so that connection tracking is disabled for the host (VE0). It does this with `options nf_conntrack ip_conntrack_disable_ve0=1` in /etc/modprobe.d. With conntrack disabled on the host, the nat table is unavailable even though the modules are loaded. Fix: Find the setting with `grep -R "ip_conntrack_disable_ve0=1" /etc/modprobe.d/` and change it to `options nf_conntrack ip_conntrack_disable_ve0=0`. Then reboot, or unload the modules in this order so they reload with the new option: iptable_nat, nf_nat, nf_conntrack_ipv4, nf_conntrack.
solution: (1) The problem was introduced by the vzctl 4.7 update, not by the kernel. (2) vzctl 4.7 disables conntrack for VE0 (the host) by default, for venet performance reasons. (3) The nf_conntrack module option ip_conntrack_disable_ve0=1 is set in /etc/modprobe.d. (4) Set the option to 0 and reload the conntrack/nat modules or reboot.

grounding.title: iptables nat does not exist

question:
Dev workstation running Mac OS X Lion with the bundled Apache2, a separately installed MySQL server, PHP and phpMyAdmin. PHP database connections only succeed when the host is given as "127.0.0.1". The same script fails to connect when the host is "localhost". Nothing else in the script changes between the two cases: same user, same password, same database. The server is clearly up and accepting connections. Running mysqladmin with its option dump shows the effective client settings: host (No default value), port 0, socket (No default value), user (No default value), connect-timeout 43200, and ssl FALSE. No my.cnf customizations have been made beyond the defaults. The operator is puzzled why the two hostnames, which should mean the same machine, behave differently.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: MySQL clients treat the host "localhost" specially and connect through the Unix domain socket file instead of TCP. 127.0.0.1 forces a TCP/IP connection. The server and clients have no working, agreed-upon socket path configured (socket shows no value), so socket connections fail while TCP works. Fix: Set the socket path explicitly in my.cnf, for example under [mysqld]: socket=/var/lib/mysql/mysql.sock (with matching datadir). Make sure clients and PHP use the same socket path, then restart the MySQL server.
solution: (1) 'localhost' makes the MySQL client use the Unix socket, not TCP (2) 127.0.0.1 forces a TCP/IP network connection, which is why it works (3) The socket option is unset/misconfigured, so the socket file isn't where clients expect (4) Configure socket= in my.cnf and restart mysqld

grounding.title: MySQL cannot connect via "localhost", only 127.0.0.1

question:
We are moving a few Upstart job definitions from Ubuntu servers to Amazon Linux instances running under Elastic Beanstalk. Not even a trivial test job will start.

As root I created /etc/init/test.conf:

```
description "test"
start on startup
script
 echo $(ping -c 1 serverfault.com) > /var/log/testjob.log
end script
```

Starting it fails:

```
# sudo service test start
test: unrecognized service
```

The same file works without changes on our Ubuntu boxes. Every Upstart job we have tried on the Amazon Linux instance gives the same 'unrecognized service' message.

What I've seen online says this usually means a syntax error in the job file. That doesn't seem to fit, because the file parses and runs on Ubuntu. No log file is produced on Amazon Linux. I need a working way to start these jobs.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: On Amazon Linux the `service` command does not recognize or dispatch to Upstart jobs defined in /etc/init. It reports 'unrecognized service' even though the job file is valid and Upstart itself can run it. Fix: Control the job with Upstart's own tool instead of `service`: run `sudo initctl start test`, which returns 'test start/running, process NNNN'. Use `sudo initctl list` to see job states and check /var/log/messages for errors.
solution: (1) The job file syntax is valid; the error does not come from Upstart parsing. (2) The `service` wrapper on Amazon Linux does not handle Upstart jobs in /etc/init. (3) Using `initctl start <job>` starts the job successfully. (4) `initctl list` and /var/log/messages help verify job status and errors.
technology: Amazon Linux / Upstart on AWS EC2 (Elastic Beanstalk)

grounding.title: EC2 linux any and all upstart jobs returning "unrecognised service"

question:
We're copying backup files between two servers with scp. Both run sshd on port 222 with identical sshd_config (root login disabled, PasswordAuthentication yes). Key-based auth is not an option for us. Copying from server A to server B while logged into A works fine. Copying from B to A while logged into B fails right away with 'Permission denied'. It never prompts for a password.

Command run on B:
  scp -P 222 -vvv ~/backup/file user@serverA:/home/user/backup

Tail of verbose output:
  debug1: SSH2_MSG_SERVICE_ACCEPT received
  debug3: send packet: type 50
  debug3: receive packet: type 51
  debug1: Authentications that can continue: password
  debug3: start over, passed a different list password
  debug3: preferred publickey,keyboard-interactive
  debug1: No more authentication methods to try.
  user@serverA: Permission denied (password).

The server clearly lists password as allowed, so why is there no prompt?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The SSH client on server B is set to prefer only publickey and keyboard-interactive. Server A offers only password. With no method in common, the client gives up without prompting. Fix: Allow password authentication on the client side, for example by running scp with -o PreferredAuthentications=password, or by fixing the client's ssh_config PreferredAuthentications setting. Ideally, also re-enable publickey authentication.
solution: (1) Server A accepts only 'password' (Authentications that can continue: password) (2) Client B's preferred methods are publickey,keyboard-interactive, which excludes password (3) No method overlaps, so the client reports no more methods to try and never prompts (4) Fix by passing -o PreferredAuthentications=password or adjusting the client config

grounding.title: SCP with password authentication only doesn't ask me for password

question:
New home server (HP ProLiant MicroServer) running Arch Linux, kernel 3.2.12. eth0 is the WAN NIC (onboard Broadcom BCM5723) and eth1 is the LAN NIC (Intel 82574L PCIe). The goal is to share the internet connection with the LAN.

Steps taken so far:
- Installed iptables 1.4.12.2.
- Set net.ipv4.ip_forward=1.
- Enabled forwarding in the iptables config file, following common NAT gateway guides (Arch wiki stateful firewall/NAT, and others).
- Rebooted.

After the reboot the box can't use any of its interfaces. Every ping from the server fails with:

  ping: sendmsg: Operation not permitted

With the iptables package removed entirely, networking works normally: the server reaches the internet and LAN hosts can SSH in. The same guide-based approach worked fine on a previous server. Why does the server lose all connectivity once the firewall rules are active?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The loaded iptables ruleset gives the OUTPUT chain a restrictive policy (DROP) and no rules allowing the needed traffic. The kernel therefore refuses locally generated packets such as ICMP echo, and sendmsg returns EPERM ("Operation not permitted"). Fix: Allow outgoing traffic from the box. Either set the OUTPUT policy to ACCEPT (`iptables -P OUTPUT ACCEPT`), or keep the DROP policy and add explicit ACCEPT rules for the required traffic. Review the INPUT and FORWARD chain policies and rules the same way, so that NAT/forwarded and inbound traffic is also permitted.
solution: (1) "sendmsg: Operation not permitted" means a local netfilter rule or policy is rejecting the outgoing packet. (2) The OUTPUT chain policy is DROP, or it has no rules allowing the server's own traffic. (3) Fix by setting the OUTPUT policy to ACCEPT, or by adding selective ACCEPT rules. (4) INPUT and FORWARD chains need appropriate policies/rules as well for the gateway to work.

grounding.title: Ping: sendmsg: operation not permitted error after installing iptables on Arch GNU/Linux

question:
We have a LEMP stack running PHP 7.0. The nginx server block hands PHP requests to FPM over a Unix socket:

```
fastcgi_pass unix:/var/run/php/php7.0-fpm.sock;
```

Every page load returns 502 Bad Gateway. The nginx error log shows this on each request:

```
*1 connect() to unix:/var/run/php/php7.0-fpm.sock failed (13: Permission denied) while connecting to upstream, client: x.x.x.x, server: example.com, request: "GET / HTTP/1.1", upstream: "fastcgi://unix:/var/run/php/php7.0-fpm.sock:", host: "example.com"
```

The socket file exists, and php7.0-fpm is running. The error says permission denied. I have looked around but can't tell which object needs which permission, or for whom.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The PHP-FPM pool creates the socket owned by www-data:www-data with mode 0660. nginx runs as a different user (nginx), so its workers cannot open the socket. Fix: Make the users match. Either set listen.owner and listen.group in /etc/php/7.0/fpm/pool.d/www.conf to the nginx user, or change the `user` directive in /etc/nginx/nginx.conf to www-data. Then restart php-fpm and nginx.
solution: (1) nginx worker user (nginx) differs from the FPM socket owner (www-data) (2) The socket mode 0660 denies access to users other than the owner and group (3) Settings to check: listen.owner, listen.group and listen.mode in pool.d/www.conf, and the user directive in nginx.conf (4) Align the users or groups, then restart the services

grounding.title: Permission Denied for fastcgi_pass using PHP7

question:
An operator is using an SSH dynamic port forward as a SOCKS5 proxy for Firefox. The session was started with `ssh user@xx.yy.zz.41 -p 1234 -D 9898`, and Firefox is set to use SOCKS5 at 127.0.0.1:9898. Browsing works and pages load normally.

The terminal running the SSH session keeps printing bursts of messages every so often:
```
channel 39: open failed: connect failed: Connection timed out
channel 41: open failed: connect failed: Connection timed out
channel 42: open failed: connect failed: Connection timed out
channel 43: open failed: connect failed: Connection timed out
channel 44: open failed: connect failed: Connection timed out
```
The messages clutter the shell and the screen session. The operator wants to know what they mean, whether something is broken, and what to do about them.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: Each browser request through the SOCKS proxy opens a new SSH channel, and the SSH server then connects out to the target web host. Some of those outbound HTTP connections time out because the destination server is overloaded or badly configured, and SSH reports each failed channel open on the client terminal. The tunnel itself is fine. Fix: Treat the messages as harmless warnings. To keep them from cluttering the terminal or screen session, start SSH in quiet mode with `ssh user@xx.yy.zz.41 -p 1234 -D 9898 -q`, which suppresses most warning and diagnostic messages.
solution: (1) Each SOCKS request through -D opens a separate SSH channel, and the server connects onward to the destination host (2) The 'open failed: connect failed: Connection timed out' message means the server-side connection to some destination timed out, often due to remote server load or misconfiguration (3) The tunnel itself is working, and the messages are benign (4) The -q (quiet) option suppresses these diagnostic messages

grounding.title: strange output on ssh tunneling: output failed; connect failed: Connection timed out;

answer: Root cause: The proxy location sets no failover behaviour and no short connect timeout. nginx therefore does not promptly detect that the stopped upstream is unavailable. Requests routed to it hang until the default connect timeout expires, instead of failing fast and being retried on the other server. Fix: Add `proxy_next_upstream error timeout invalid_header http_500;` to the location so failed requests are retried on the next upstream server. Also set a short `proxy_connect_timeout` (e.g. 2 seconds) so a dead backend is detected quickly.
solution: (1) nginx is not quickly detecting the downed upstream, so requests to it hang until timeout (2) proxy_next_upstream controls which failure conditions (error, timeout, invalid_header, http_500) cause a retry on another upstream (3) proxy_connect_timeout should be lowered (e.g. 2s) so connection attempts to a dead backend fail fast

grounding.title: nginx automatic failover load balancing

question:
We have a nightly backup job on a Windows server that runs:

mysqldump -u user -p"pass" --lock-tables --default-character-set=latin1 -e --quick databasename > "query.sql"

It now fails every time with:

mysqldump: Got error: 23: Out of resources when opening file '.\db\sometable.MYD' (Errcode: 24) when using LOCK TABLES

The failure always names the same table. Restarting the MySQL service did not change anything. I lowered table_cache from 64 to 32 and max_connections from 30 to 10. The error still happens, but it now names a different table, and it names that second table every time since the change. The same script runs without problems on about a dozen other Windows servers that hold the same database, and each database has 85 tables. What is going wrong on this one server, and how should I fix it?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: Errcode 24 is the OS error "Too many open files". The MySQL server is running out of file handles. When mysqldump uses --lock-tables, it locks and opens all of the database's tables at the same time. On this server that exceeds the number of files the MySQL process is allowed to open. Fix: Raise MySQL's open_files_limit setting (--open-files-limit), along with any OS-level limit, so the server can open enough file handles. Alternatively, run the dump with --single-transaction instead of --lock-tables, ideally while nobody else is using the database, so tables are not all opened at once. If the problem continues, look for other processes on this server that are using up file handles.
solution: (1) Error 23 / Errcode 24 means too many open files (file handle exhaustion), not memory (2) --lock-tables opens all tables simultaneously, consuming many file handles (3) Increase open_files_limit (--open-files-limit) for mysqld (4) Use --single-transaction instead of --lock-tables to reduce simultaneously open files

grounding.title: Out of resources for mysqldump

question:
I'm on a Windows 7 workstation. I unpacked the mysql-5.7.9 zip to C:\mysql-5.7.9 so I can run it as a second, self-contained instance alongside an older MySQL that is already running. I registered a service with:
"C:\mysql-5.7.9\bin\mysqld.exe" --install mysql579 --defaults-file="C:\mysql-5.7.9\bin\my.cnf"

The my.cnf sets basedir=C:/mysql-5.7.9, datadir=C:/mysql-5.7.9/data and tmpdir=C:/mysql-5.7.9/tmp. It also sets port 3307, socket mysql579, server-id 2 and latin1 charset/collation.

The service won't start correctly. Startup fails with "Can't open and lock privilege tables: Table 'mysql.user' doesn't exist".

To debug, I ran mysqld.exe --defaults-file=... --standalone --console. InnoDB starts normally, creates ibtmp1 and loads the buffer pool from C:\mysql-5.7.9\data. After that I get:
- "mysqld: Table 'mysql.plugin' doesn't exist"
- "[ERROR] Can't open the mysql.plugin table. Please run mysql_upgrade to create it."
- "[Warning] Gtid table is not ready to be used. Table 'mysql.gtid_executed' cannot be opened."

There are also warnings about TIMESTAMP defaults, secure-file-priv and SSL certificates.

Why can't the new instance find its system tables?

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: Starting with MySQL 5.7.7, the distribution no longer ships a pre-populated data directory with the mysql system database (user, plugin and similar tables). The new instance's data directory was never initialized, so those tables don't exist. Fix: Initialize the data directory before starting the server. Run mysqld --initialize --console, using the same defaults file/datadir as the service. This creates the system tables and the initial root account. Then start the service.
solution: (1) MySQL 5.7.7+ does not include initial data or system tables in the distribution (2) The data directory must be initialized with mysqld --initialize (or --initialize-insecure) (3) The missing mysql.user / mysql.plugin tables come from an uninitialized datadir, not from a port or socket conflict with the other instance

grounding.title: Can't open and lock privilege tables: Table 'mysql.user' doesn't exist - Trying to run second instance of myslq

question:
Setting up HTTPS on Apache 2.2.16 / Ubuntu 10.10. Apache fails at startup with:

[error] Init: Unable to read server certificate from file /etc/apache2/mysite.com.ssl/mysite.com.crt/mysite.com.crt
[error] SSL Library Error: 218529960 error:0D0680A8:asn1 encoding routines:ASN1_CHECK_TLEN:wrong tag
[error] SSL Library Error: 218595386 error:0D07803A:asn1 encoding routines:ASN1_ITEM_EX_D2I:nested asn1 error

The certificate text was pasted from the CA's confirmation email, which I read on my workstation before transferring the file to the server. It has the header and footer lines; grep '^-----' shows exactly -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- and -----END CERTIFICATE-----. Even so, OpenSSL can't parse it:

openssl x509 -noout -text -in mysite.com.crt -> unable to load certificate ... PEM_read_bio:no start line:pem_lib.c:650:Expecting: TRUSTED CERTIFICATE
Same error with -inform PEM. With -inform DER: ASN1_CHECK_TLEN:wrong tag / nested asn1 error Type=X509.

The CA checked the CSR, says it is fine, and suggested I was using the wrong filename in the command. The filename is correct. Looking for what's actually wrong with the file.

What is the most likely root cause, and how would you fix it?
answer: Root cause: The certificate file was saved/transferred with Windows-style line endings, so every line ends in a carriage return (^M). The older OpenSSL/Apache versions in use can't parse PEM data with CRLF line endings. Fix: Check with `vi -b` (or similar) for ^M at the end of each line. Strip them using dos2unix, or by editing the file, or re-transfer the file in Unix line-ending format, then restart Apache.
solution: (1) The PEM file has CRLF (^M) line endings from Windows (2) Older OpenSSL/Apache fails to parse the PEM even though BEGIN/END markers are present (3) Inspect with vi -b or similar to see the ^M characters (4) Convert with dos2unix or re-transfer the file correctly

grounding.title: SSL Error - unable to read server certificate from file

question:
Hardened Linux box running OpenSSH. Password authentication is disabled and only public keys are accepted. No Java runtime is installed anywhere on the host.
